jobs.description:
Job Description

We aspire to be the premier research-intensive biopharmaceutical company. We're at the forefront of research to deliver innovative health solutions that advance the prevention and treatment of diseases in people and animals. Join our company and be part of a team that uses the power of leading-edge science to save and improve lives around the world.

Within Small Molecule Science & Technology (SM S&T), we are advancing digital and data capabilities that strengthen technical operations, accelerate insight generation, and improve business outcomes across the product lifecycle. The Director, Data Engineering and Analytics is a newly created and exciting role, and we are looking for a data-minded engineer to join Small Molecule Science and Technology (SMS&T) to lead and build a data engineering and analytics team across Technical Operations.

The Director of Data Engineering and Analytics, reporting to the Executive Director or End to End Technical Leadership Organization, will serve as the technical leader responsible for translating Small Molecule Science & Technology's (SM S&T) data and analytics priorities into execution, adoption, and business value. This role requires who can drive accountability and execution across a highly matrixed organization across SM S&T, Digital Manufacturing Division, Digital CMC, MPI, IT and Global Pharmaceutical Operations to accelerate the deployment, implementation and standardization of digital strategy tools to advance analytics and data engineering capabilities, deliver sustained adoption and measurable business impact.

The Director is expected to bring a strong understating of digital systems and tools, data science and analytics operating effectively at the intersection of business, science, manufacturing, engineering, and digital technology. The role requires a strong technical understanding of unit operations across Small Molecule Drug Substance, Drug Product, Packaging, and Analytical Sciences to maximize value add to the pipeline and inline portfolio.

Responsibilities

Drive execution of agreed-upon data and analytics priorities across Small Molecule Science & Technology (SM S&T), ensuring progress and measurable business impact.
Translate data and analytics strategy into practical implementation plans, clear milestones, and value realization metrics.
Partner with SM S&T leadership, Digital Manufacturing Division, Digital CMC, MPI, IT, and site teams to align priorities and remove barriers to execution.
Ensure analytics initiatives are anchored in clear business problems and deliver practical value to the organization.
Serve as a credible translator between technical SMEs, manufacturing teams, and data/IT partners.
Convert complex business and manufacturing needs into practical analytical requirements and scalable solution designs.
Influence the data and analytics strategy across partner organizations where alignment is required.
Advance the democratization and engineering of data across SM S&T by improving the access, contextualization, and usability of manufacturing and process data.
Lead data engineering initiatives to build robust data pipelines, ensuring data quality and accessibility from source systems to analytical platforms.
Enable scientists and engineers to directly access and use data to support process monitoring, investigations, and lifecycle management.
Drive adoption of capabilities that support Proactive Process Monitoring, Continuous Process Verification, Manufacturing Process Intelligence (MPI), and data-driven decision-making.
Lead the implementation and adoption of data and analytics solutions across SM S&T.
Apply a strong technical understanding of unit operations across Drug Substance, Drug Product, Packaging, and analytical to ensure analytical tools are effectively utilized across the portfolio.
Establish and strengthen user communities to scale adoption beyond centralized expertise.
Represent SM S&T business priorities in data governance, portfolio, and demand management forums.
Partner with leadership to define the highest-value use cases and ensure resources are focused on impactful priorities.
Track progress against priorities and hold teams accountable for delivery, adoption, and value realization.

Qualifications

Required

Bachelor of Science (BS) in Engineering, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Data Science, Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related technical discipline with ten (10) years of required experience. (MS with 8)
Demonstrated leadership in pharmaceutical manufacturing, technical operations, data engineering, or data science, with a proven track record of driving data-driven transformation in a regulated environment.
Deep understanding of pharmaceutical manufacturing processes, including a strong technical understanding of unit operations across Drug Substance, Drug Product, packaging, and analytical.
Expertise in manufacturing data systems, process monitoring, and data and analytics technologies supporting technical operations.
Proven ability to influence across matrix organizations and drive accountability for execution and results.

Experience with manufacturing data and analytics platforms such as DataLynx, SEEQ, MPI, MES, historians, or similar technologies.

Leads the engineering teams which includes but not exclusive to managing, coaching, and evaluating the Video Engineering team and the Audio Engineering team.

Manages projects, vendors, and resources. Defines project requirements, evaluates vendors, manage approved expenditures, and oversees installation, commissioning, acceptance testing, and handover.
Maintain engineering standards by creating documentation, inventory, access, and configuration standards.
Coordinates broadcast network changes with IT, maintain drawings and procedures, and uses incident trends to prioritize training and system improvements.

CANDIDATE PROFILE: Who You Are

The ideal candidate brings deep broadcast engineering expertise, strong technical leadership, and the ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced live event environment.

Minimum 10 years of broadcast engineering or comparable live production infrastructure experience, including a minimum of three years supervising technical staff and leading engineering projects, maintenance programs, and/or event support.
Demonstrated ability to design, support, and troubleshoot SMPTE ST 2110 systems, including PTP synchronization, multicast traffic, IP addressing, VLANs, network redundancy, and interfaces between IP and SDI systems.
Strong understanding of switchers, routers, replay/playback, cameras, broadcast audio, intercom, tally/control, and monitoring, with working familiarity with lighting interfaces.
Ability to interpret and create engineering/CAD drawings and establish accurate signal-flow, cabling, and system documentation.
Ability to develop budgets, evaluate technical proposals, manage vendors and implementation schedules, and make equipment lifecycle recommendations based on operational needs, reliability, and available resources.
Sound judgment under live event pressure, with the ability to explain technical decisions clearly, resolve competing priorities, train staff, and collaborate with internal partners, visiting production teams, multiple trades, and union crews.
Ability to work flexible schedules as needed to support live events, urgent technical issues, maintenance windows, and last-minute schedule adjustments. The role regularly requires nights, weekends, and holidays, including extended days, late nights, and early mornings, and may include on-call support for time-sensitive technical needs.
You’re a team player, highly motivated, and have an eye for production best practices
You’re self-starter, works well independently, and collaborates in a team environment

Broadcast Engineering & SMPTE ST 2110

jobs.title: Chief Technology Officer
jobs.description:
Who We Are

Blackstone Law is growing fast. With nearly 50 attorneys, we’ve become one of California’s leading plaintiff side employment law firms, representing employees in individual and class action employment matters.

We’ve built a fast-moving, technology driven firm that combines experienced legal judgment with technology and automation to work smarter and deliver better outcomes for our clients. We’re looking for talented CTO Professional who are excited about the opportunity to help us grow our presence in a new market.

Our culture is collaborative, comfortable, and performance driven. We work hard, support one another, and believe you can do exceptional work while still having a life outside of it. We’re a family that values each person’s contribution and invests in their growth.

About the Role

Blackstone Law is looking for a forward-thinking, hands-on Chief Technology Officer to lead the next phase of our technology strategy.

We have already made significant investments in technology, AI, automation, and data. We’re looking for an experienced technology leader who will take us to the next level.

This is not a traditional IT leadership role. We need someone who understands how AI, data, software, infrastructure, cybersecurity, and automation work together—and can translate those capabilities into measurable improvements in how a modern law firm operates.

The CTO will partner directly with executive leadership while providing technical direction and accountability to our internal and external technology resources.

While we are primarily seeking a full-time CTO, we are open to considering the right candidate on a fractional basis initially.

What You’ll Do

Own and execute the firm’s technology, AI, data, and infrastructure strategy.

Assess our current technology environment, architecture, systems, integrations, vendors, and development initiatives and identify gaps, risks, and opportunities.

Lead the firm’s AI strategy, including the evaluation, development, implementation, and governance of AI-powered tools and workflows.

Provide technical leadership and accountability for developers, IT resources, consultants, and technology vendors.

Establish clear expectations around project scope, milestones, deliverables, timelines, and performance.

Identify opportunities to automate workflows, improve productivity, strengthen knowledge management, and better leverage firm data.

Ensure our technology environment is secure, scalable, reliable, and positioned to support continued growth.

Oversee cybersecurity, data governance, privacy, business continuity, disaster recovery, and technology risk.

Evaluate emerging technologies based on practical business value—not technology for technology’s sake.

Partner with the Leadership, attorneys, and operational leaders to translate business needs into practical technology solutions.

Own technology budgeting and help leadership make informed investment decisions.

What We’re Looking For

10+ years of progressive technology leadership experience, including CTO, CIO, VP/Head of Technology, or comparable leadership experience.
Proven experience building and executing technology strategies within a growing organization.
Strong technical knowledge across AI, data architecture, cloud infrastructure, cybersecurity, systems integration, and software development.
Hands-on experience evaluating, implementing, and scaling AI and automation solutions.
Experience leading developers, engineers, IT professionals, vendors, and outsourced technology resources.
Ability to quickly assess an existing technology environment and determine what should be scaled, improved, replaced, or rebuilt.
Strong execution and project-management discipline with a track record of turning strategy into measurable results.
Ability to communicate complex technical concepts clearly to non-technical executives and business leaders.
Experience working in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial organization.
Law firm or legal technology experience preferred; professional services experience is also highly valued.

Duties

Summary

This position is being filled under a stream-lined hiring authority, Title 21 of the United States Code (21 US Code 379d-3a) as amended by the 21st Century Cures Act of 2016, section 3072 and the Consolidated Appropriations Act of 2023, Section 3624. The candidate selected for this position will serve under a career or career-conditional appointment and be paid under the provisions of this authority. This position is being recruited based on the Title 21 Pay Table 4, Band G.

Requirements

Qualifications

In order to qualify for the Director, Office of Science and Engineering Laboratories (OSEL) position which falls under the 0801 occupational Series, you must meet the following requirements by 11:59 pm EST on 10/28/2026: The candidate must meet the following qualifications for this Title 21 position: Scientific, Technical, and/or Professional Fields Qualified and Outstanding Candidates a. Qualified applies to all candidates for Cures appointments. The FDA OTS will use the technical qualifications defined below as a baseline for comparing experience levels and other candidate attributes for relevant positions b, Outstanding candidates can be defined by existing outstanding work experience, outstanding performance rating, or both. Basic Requirements A. Degree: Engineering. To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by ABET; or (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics. OR B. Combination of education and experience -- college-level education, training, and/or technical experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, and (2) a good understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the engineering sciences and techniques and their applications to one of the branches of engineering. The adequacy of such background must be demonstrated by one of the following: 1. Professional registration or licensure -- Current registration as an Engineer Intern(EI), Engineer in Training (EIT)1, or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration. For example, an applicant who attains registration through a State Board's eminence provision as a manufacturing engineer typically would be rated eligible only for manufacturing engineering positions. 2. Written Test -- Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE)2 examination or any other written test required for professional 1 For more information about EI and EIT registration requirements, please visit the National Society of Professional Engineers website. The FE examination is not administered by the U. S. Office of Personnel Management. For more information please visit: http://www.nspe.org/Licensure/HowtoGetLicensed/index.html.2 registration by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico. 3. Specified academic courses -- Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and that included the courses specified in the basic requirements under paragraph A. The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program as described in paragraph A. 4. Related curriculum -- Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, maybe accepted in lieu of a bachelor's degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance. Ordinarily there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience, e.g.in interdisciplinary positions. Desired Qualifications: Possesses a Ph.D. in the life sciences or an M.D./Ph.D. degree, with advanced research and scientific training relevant to the position. The preferred qualification reflects the depth of research expertise needed to lead multidisciplinary regulatory science programs and address complex scientific and emerging technologies. An M.D. without a Ph.D. is not considered equivalent to the preferred research and scientific background. This position is designated as an SES Equivalent position and is covered under the FDA Title 21 Executive Performance Management System and identified as a public filing position for ethics purposes. While PHS Commissioned Corps Officers cannot hold a Title 21 position during their active service as PHS Officers, we welcome and encourage them to apply-their applications will receive full consideration. Please note that if selected, the Officer will need to end their Commissioned Corps appointment before being placed in the Title 21 position. Supervisory Responsibilities The incumbent is delegated full authority to achieve group goals and objectives through the effective management of available resources. Performance and accomplishments are assessed primarily through work performance indicators, staff discussion, planning sessions, review of individual project outputs, and annual program review. Leads in a proactive, customer-responsive manner consistent with Agency vision and values, effectively communicating program issues to external audiences. Ensures financial and managerial accountability by acting with prudence when executing fiduciary responsibilities. Demonstrates high integrity and adheres to the highest ethical standards of public service. Uses effective business practices including balanced measures of results, values, and invests in each employee; emphasizes empowerment and two-way communication. Takes a leadership role in advocating for and advancing the priorities of the Agency. Serves as a role model for leadership by encouraging teamwork and a collaborative approach. Timely notifies Agency officials of all significant actions and developments, including but not limited to those related to regulatory matters, legislative matters, budget matters, reports, initiatives, and events and ensures subordinate managers do the same. Provides reasonable accommodations needed to best utilize qualified people with disabilities. Organizational Management: Manages the Office of Science and Engineering Laboratories (OSEL) within CDRH Program Management: Runs a multidisciplinary regulatory science program in the Center encompassing multiple laboratories and scientific disciplines. Directs and evaluates activities addressing scientific and technical questions relevant to medical devices and radiation-emitting products, including test methods, biocompatibility, biological testing, in vitro/in vivo evaluation, computational modeling, and reference materials. Resource Management: Monitors and reports on resources needed to lead strategic resource planning for OSEL and its multidisciplinary regulatory science programs. Establishes annual and multi-year objectives, determines program priorities, and allocates resources across OSEL's scientific programs. Human Capital Management: Identifies employee competencies necessary to meet OSEL's organizational capabilities goals across its multidisciplinary scientific workforce. Designs competency frameworks and workforce architecture to ensure OSEL maintains the scientific capabilities needed for current and emerging regulatory science challenges.

jobs.description:
Job Responsibilities

Supervises the encroachment permits review/approval process for commercial and large residential developments within the District. Reviews permits in a timely manner for accuracy, supporting documentation, and compliance with SCDOT engineering standards, policies, and guidelines. Coordinates with county offices and various engineering divisions within SCDOT in review of permits as necessary.

Coordinates reviews by, and/or meetings with developers, local officials, district engineers, headquarters staff, etc., on complex encroachment permits to discuss and ensure compliance with state and federal engineering standards and to resolve problems related to permit approval and compliance. Conducts site visits as required for preliminary review and consideration of encroachment permits.

Reviews encroachment permits submitted by local governments and public agencies. Serves as the district liaison for the coordination of submittals and plan reviews pertaining to the proposed roadway improvement, design and enhancements. Collects comments from appropriate Agency engineering disciplines and provides a single response to applicant.

Maintains encroachment permit files and tracking system for the district to ensure timely review and processing. Initiates and coordinates review of permits by various units within SCDOT as required by policy. Coordinates site inspections on approved encroachment permits as necessary to ensure compliance with permit design, special provisions, safety and workmanship. Reviews other encroachment permits submitted to the District Office by county offices as necessary. Provides support and direction on complex permit design, construction sequencing, traffic control, etc. Provides support and training of county encroachment permit technicians related to encroachment permit standards and regulations as necessary. Assists with emergency and inclement weather operations, may include extended hours and/or 12-hour shifts.

Minimum And Additional Requirements

A bachelor’s degree in Engineering and six (6) years of engineering work experience. Necessary Special Requirement: Registration as a Professional Engineer by the South Carolina State Board of Registration for Professional Engineers and Surveyors.

The physical demands for the essential functions involves sitting or standing at a desk for extended periods of time. This position may require occasional travel. May require bending, stooping, reaching, twisting, climbing, balancing, and kneeling. Walking for extended periods, treading rough terrain, working in close proximity to motoring traffic, and in natural environmental hazards. May be required to work outside normal business hours or respond to emergency situations.

Additional Comments

A resume may be included but NOT substituted for completing the education, work experience, or any other sections of the application. Supplemental Questions are considered part of the application and must be completed.

Non-Discrimination Statement:
The South Carolina Department of Transportation is committed to a diverse workforce and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy), national origin, age (40 or older), disability or genetic information. May be required to work overtime, nighttime, and/or weekends during hazardous weather or emergencies.

jobs.title: Technology Director — Global Health (REMOTE ROLE)
jobs.description:
Description

Technology Director — Global Health

ICF's Global Health and Development (GHD) line of business, part of the Health, People, and Human Services (HPHS) Group, is seeking a Technology Director
to lead technology modernization efforts across various global health and survey programs. This is a hands-on leadership role. You will own delivery of the program's technology work from end to end. You will also serve as one of its technical leads and architects, designing systems yourself as well as directing the team that builds them. You will bridge ICF's applied AI and software engineers with its survey methodologists, statisticians, field operations staff, and country partners. You will be accountable to the funder for results, including the decision to redirect work that isn't performing and move the funding to work that is.

This position can be remote within the United States, with occasional international travel.

It is contingent upon award of program funding.

Key Responsibilities

Technology Modernization Delivery Leadership

Own delivery of the program's AI innovation portfolio. The workstreams cover automated data-to-report production, natural-language data access, multilingual questionnaire design, field data quality, and new measurement approaches.
Run the stage-gate process. Lead go/no-go reviews, and make and defend decisions to stop workstreams, publish what they learned, and reallocate their funding.
Serve as the principal technical counterpart to the funder. Lead progress reporting and learning reviews. Communicate results candidly, including negative ones.
Manage the innovation portfolio, schedule, and risks with the project manager, including inference and cloud operating costs.
Coordinate across global development programs. Share successes, failures, and methods with technology partners to avoid duplicating work.

Technical Leadership & Architecture

Act as technical lead and architect for a cluster of workstreams. Own their system design, write the design documents, and stay hands-on through prototyping and production.
Define acceptance criteria before the work is judged. With survey experts, set the quantitative quality thresholds each tool must meet, and hold the team (and yourself) to them.
Set architecture and standards across the portfolio: model selection and routing, privacy-preserving design, offline and low-connectivity deployment, and security.
Set engineering practice for the team, including specification-driven development with agentic coding tools, evaluation-first delivery, code review, and testing.
Protect data quality and comparability. Work with survey methodologists so that no innovation breaks the comparability of data across countries and over time.
Oversee responsible AI, data governance, and ethics. Make sure the program meets ICF security standards, IRB requirements, and partner-country data sovereignty expectations.

Team Leadership & Collaboration

Lead and mentor the program's technology team, including applied AI, software, ML, and platform engineers.
Bridge technology and survey expertise. Make sure survey methodologists, statisticians, and field teams shape what gets built, and that engineers understand how surveys work.
Work with national statistical offices and ministries of health, together with ICF's country engagement leads, to design tools that countries want and can run on their own.
Share the program's results openly through public documentation, publications, and presentations at technical and global health conferences.
Contribute to business growth efforts including proactive engagement with potential clients, preparation of white papers, and proposal development.

Minimum Required Experience

Bachelors degree in IT, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related technical field (or equivalent experience)
Minimum 10 years of professional experience designing and delivering technology solutions, including hands-on architecture of multiple complex systems taken into production
Minimum 5 years leading and mentoring software or data engineering teams to build products or deploy systems

Additional Required Skills And Experience

A track record of architecting and delivering AI/ML or LLM-powered systems in production, and the ability to explain how their quality was measured and where they failed
Experience leading a multi-workstream technology program for a foundation, donor, or government client, with accountability for budget and results
Deep knowledge of system architecture, data pipelines, software development methods, and at least one major cloud platform (e.g., AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud)
Hands-on familiarity with agentic coding tools and specification-driven development, and experience setting how a team uses them
U.S. citizenship is required by federal government contract

Preferred Skills

Working proficiency in French or Portuguese
Background in survey operations or data collection, such as work on or with the Demographic & Health Surveys (DHS) Program, Multiple Indicator Cluster Surveys (MICS), Living Standards Measurement Study (LSMS), a national census, or other population-based household surveys
Experience delivering technology for global health or international development programs in low- and middle-income countries
Experience with field data-collection systems for low-connectivity settings (e.g., e, c, ODK), or with offline or edge deployment
Experience working with national statistical offices or ministries of health
Experience leading a stage-gated R&D or innovation portfolio, including a decision to stop a workstream
Experience setting and being held to quantitative acceptance thresholds for an AI or data system
Experience with multi-country deployments where data cannot leave a jurisdiction, and with data privacy and governance for human data, including IRB processes
Experience with cybersecurity practices, security controls, and authorization processes
Publications or conference presentations in AI, survey methods, or global health
Advanced degree in computer science, statistics, demography, public health, or a related field

Professional Skills

Credible with both engineers and executives. Can lead a technical design review in the morning and brief a funder's leadership in the afternoon
Sound judgment under uncertainty. Can tell a workstream that is late from one that isn't going to work, and acts on it
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to translate between technical and non-technical stakeholders, including survey experts and government partners
Strong presentation skills, with the ability to simplify complex topics for business, funder, and program audiences
Works productively and builds relationships at all levels and across cultures, from senior leadership to entry level
Self-motivated. Finds ways to add value without a lot of direct supervision

jobs.description:
Repligen is seeking a Senior Service Systems, Infrastructure & Analytics Manager to lead the systems, data infrastructure, integrations, and analytics that support our rapidly growing global service organization. Reporting to the VP, Service, this role sits at the intersection of technology, data, and service operations, partnering across Service, IT, Commercial Operations, Finance, Quality, and Field Service to build scalable solutions that drive business performance, operational excellence, and customer success.

This role is expected to model our Leadership Behaviors—Integrity & Compliance, Customer Focus, Collaboration, Courage, Team Empowerment, and Accountability & Results—in all aspects of work.

Responsibilities

Partner with service leadership to define, document, and continuously improve global service business processes, standards, and best practices.
Translate business needs and user experiences into clear system requirements and scalable technical solutions that support the long-term growth of the service business.
Lead the design, configuration, implementation, maintenance, and optimization of service business systems and infrastructure on a global scale.
Design, manage, and enhance integrations between Salesforce, SAP, internally developed service applications, reporting platforms, and other business systems.
Develop and execute a service master data strategy, ensuring data integrity, governance, consistency, and accessibility across systems.
Build, maintain, and continuously improve dashboards, reports, and KPI frameworks that enable data-driven decision making and provide leaders with clear visibility into business performance.
Develop reporting and visualization solutions using Power BI, Tableau, and related analytics tools to deliver meaningful operational and strategic insights.
Create and manage data flows, queries, automations, and reporting structures that transform data from multiple sources into actionable business intelligence.
Act as a trusted partner to Service, IT, Commercial Operations, Finance, Quality, and Field Service teams, building strong relationships and aligning stakeholders around shared business objectives.
Provide technical guidance and business context to IT and development teams, helping prioritize enhancements, solve complex challenges, and identify opportunities for innovation.
Promote consistency and operational excellence by driving adoption of global processes, systems, and reporting methodologies across the organization.
Develop training materials, user documentation, and support programs that empower users and enable successful adoption of systems and tools.
Evaluate emerging technologies and analytics capabilities, proactively identifying opportunities to improve efficiency, scalability, visibility, and the overall customer experience.
Take ownership of strategic initiatives from concept through implementation, driving measurable outcomes through collaboration, influence, and continuous improvement.
Help shape the future of the Service Systems, Infrastructure & Analytics function by contributing to team development, process maturity, and long-term organizational success.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, Business Information Systems, or a related field.
7+ years of experience in business systems, analytics, systems architecture, service operations technology, or related disciplines.
Experience supporting field service, technical service, customer support, or equipment-based service organizations.
Strong experience with enterprise platforms such as Salesforce, SAP, Power BI, Tableau, and related business systems.
Proven experience designing system integrations, APIs, data flows, reporting frameworks, and business process automation.
Experience developing dashboards, KPIs, and analytics solutions that support operational and strategic decision-making.
Strong understanding of data architecture, master data management, data governance, and data quality best practices.
Working knowledge of SQL, Python, Power Query, DAX, Power Automate, C#, HTML, or similar scripting and automation tools.
Demonstrated ability to translate business requirements into scalable technical solutions and measurable business outcomes.
Proven success leading cross-functional initiatives and influencing stakeholders across Service, IT, Commercial Operations, Finance, and Quality organizations.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, communication, and collaboration skills, with a customer-focused mindset and a commitment to continuous improvement.

What Repligen Offers

Our mission is to inspire advances in bioprocessing as a trusted partner in the production of biologic drugs that improve human health worldwide. Focused on cost and process efficiencies, we deliver innovative technologies and solutions that help set new standards in bioprocessing. The estimated base salary range for this role, based in the United States of America is $134,000-$192,000. Compensation decisions are dependent on several factors including, but not limited to an individual's ,qualifications, location, internal equity, and alignment with market data. jobs.title: Software Engineering, Senior Director
jobs.description:
At Freddie Mac, our mission of Making Home Possible is what motivates us, and it’s at the core of everything we do. Since our charter in 1970, we have made home possible for more than 90 million families across the country. Join an organization where your work contributes to a greater purpose.

Position Overview:

Do you want your engineering leadership to shape how an entire enterprise puts generative AI to work — safely, at scale, and for real impact? At Freddie Mac, our mission of Making Home Possible is at the core of everything we do, and our Corporate Technology Strategy team is building FredAI, our internal enterprise GenAI platform and portfolio of AI-enabled products. We're searching for a hands-on, visionary engineering leader to own the technical strategy and delivery that turns cutting-edge foundation models into measurable business outcomes. Apply now and learn why there's #MoreAtFreddieMac!

Our Impact:

We build the secure, scalable platforms and reusable services that bring generative AI capabilities — including the company's internal chatbot and AI-enabled products — to teams across the enterprise.
We translate the Freddie Mac CIO vision for GenAI into an executable engineering roadmap, setting the reference architectures, standards, and shared frameworks that let multiple product teams deliver consistently and responsibly.
We partner across Architecture, Cybersecurity, Data, Model Risk, and Cloud Engineering to ensure every solution meets enterprise expectations for identity, data protection, auditability, resiliency, and responsible AI.

Your Impact:

In this role, you will be an integral part of our GenAI engineering leadership and will be expected to:

Lead the end-to-end engineering strategy, architecture, and delivery of FredAI, building production GenAI applications using foundation models, RAG, embeddings, vector search, orchestration, tool calling, and agentic workflows.
Build a reusable platform of reference architectures, SDKs, shared services, APIs, and integration patterns that accelerate delivery across multiple product teams.
Implement rigorous evaluation, testing, and LLMOps practices — offline benchmarks, regression suites, groundedness and hallucination measures, CI/CD, versioning, observability, tracing, incident response, and rollback.
Engineer secure, permission-aware solutions that enforce identity, entitlements, data boundaries, privacy, human approvals, audit logging, and responsible AI policies.
Define model and platform integration patterns, including model selection and routing, structured outputs, caching, rate limiting, fallback strategies, token budgets, circuit-breaker controls, and cost management.
Partner with cloud, platform, data, and security teams, and with the GenAI Program Manager, to integrate GenAI services with enterprise systems and translate business needs into governed, high-value capabilities.
Lead, coach, and grow a high-performing, multidisciplinary team of GenAI, software, platform, and quality engineers, setting clear expectations, career paths, and a culture of ownership and experimentation.
Manage engineering and product-quality outcomes — availability, latency, throughput, task completion, adoption, developer productivity, and cost per successful outcome.

Qualifications:

15+ years of software, data, or machine learning engineering experience, including significant technical and people leadership responsibility (4+ years leading engineering teams/managers).
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, or a related technical field, or equivalent experience (advanced degree preferred).
Proven experience architecting and delivering production GenAI or AI/ML systems at enterprise scale, with recent hands-on coding experience.
Strong proficiency in modern cloud-native engineering (Python, TypeScript/JavaScript, or Java; APIs, microservices, containers, distributed systems, CI/CD, IaC).
Hands-on knowledge of LLM application patterns — prompting, RAG, embeddings, vector search, orchestration, tool calling, agents, structured outputs, and model evaluation.
Experience designing for security, privacy, identity, data governance, resiliency, auditability, and responsible AI in a regulated enterprise environment.

Keys to Success in this Role:

A builder's mindset — you love solving the hardest engineering problems hands-on, not just directing from the sidelines.
A natural influencer who can rally engineering, security, data, risk, and business partners around a shared technical vision.
Comfortable operating in the space of "no longer" and "not yet" — translating fast-moving GenAI advances into practical, governed capabilities.
Calm under pressure, with strong operational discipline and a bias toward measurable outcomes.
A curious, continuous learner who stays current on emerging AI technologies — and a great teammate with a sense of humor.

Current Freddie Mac employees please apply through the internal career site.

We consider all applicants for all positions without regard to gender, race, color, religion, national origin, age, marital status, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity/expression, physical and mental disability, pregnancy, ethnicity, genetic information or any other protected categories under applicable federal, state or local laws. We will ensure that individuals are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodation.

This includes employee commitment to our acceptable use policy, applying a vigilance-first approach to work, supporting regulatory mandates, and using best practices to protect Freddie Mac from potential threats and risk. Employees exercise this responsibility by executing against policies and procedures and adhering to privacy & security obligations as required via training programs.

jobs.description:
At Utility, we’re reimagining what’s possible.
Our breakthrough H2Gen® technology transforms undesirable industrial by-products into clean energy and sustainable fuels and feedstocks, helping hard-to-abate industries decarbonize without compromise. We’re building systems and solutions that will power a zero-carbon future by turning what the world doesn’t want into clean energy it needs most.
But technology alone doesn’t change the world.
People do.

We’re building a team as bold as our mission. Engineers and scientists, designers and operators, storytellers and strategists all united by a shared belief: that the undesirable can become invaluable, and that industrial decarbonization can be both practical and economical.
At Utility, we see possibilities where others see limits. We believe progress happens when diverse minds collaborate toward a cleaner, smarter, more resilient world.
If you’re ready to do the most meaningful work of your career, join us and help build what’s next.
The Company

Utility Global
is redefining how the world makes and uses energy. Through its breakthrough H₂Gen® technology
, Utility transforms industrial off-gases and biogases into clean energy and sustainable fuels and feedstocks, helping industries decarbonize without compromise
. The company’s proprietary technology delivers a scalable, economic pathway to a zero-carbon future, positioning Utility as a leader in the industrial decarbonization revolution.
The Role

Utility Global is seeking a strategic, hands-on Director, Ceramic Technology
to lead our Applied Technology ceramic development team in Englewood, Colorado. Reporting to the Chief Technology Officer, this leader will set priorities, guide technical strategy, and develop the people, processes, and roadmap needed to advance ceramic materials and manufacturing technologies for high-temperature reactor components.
The ideal candidate combines deep expertise in ceramic materials and processing with proven experience leading technical teams in fast-paced R&D, pilot-scale, or manufacturing environments. This person should be comfortable translating business and technology objectives into a clear team strategy, making disciplined tradeoffs, mentoring engineers and scientists, and ensuring experimental work leads to actionable decisions and scalable process improvements.
This is a technical leadership role with accountability for both forward-looking ceramic technology development and practical manufacturing readiness. Experience in electrochemical systems is welcome, but strong leadership in ceramic materials, processing, characterization, scale-up, and technology transfer is more important than electrochemistry domain knowledge for this position.

Key Responsibilities

Lead, manage, and develop a team responsible for ceramic materials, bodies, coatings, and processes for high-temperature reactor components.
Set technical priorities, allocate resources, and translate company objectives into a focused ceramic technology roadmap.
Define and guide experimental strategy to improve performance, durability, manufacturability, quality, and cost.
Oversee the translation of bench-scale ceramic development into robust pilot-scale and manufacturing-relevant processes.
Build decision-making frameworks for powder handling, mixing, dispersion, rheology, forming, drying, thermal treatment, inspection, and related process steps.
Partner cross-functionally with R&D, engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, and external partners to select, evaluate, and qualify ceramic materials and processes.
Establish clear technical standards for testing, characterization, data analysis, documentation, and design reviews.
Guide troubleshooting and root-cause investigations for process and equipment issues affecting quality, yield, consistency, and throughput.
Support technology transfer and manufacturing readiness internally and with third-party production partners.
Communicate strategy, progress, risks, tradeoffs, and recommendations clearly to the CTO, leadership team, technical colleagues, and external stakeholders.
Ensure team activities are conducted safely and in compliance with internal procedures and relevant standards.

This role will focus primarily on building and leading a forward-looking ceramic technology function, with ongoing accountability for manufacturing support, technology transfer, and scale-up readiness across both in-house and third-party production.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications:

BS in Ceramic Engineering, Materials Science, Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field
8+ years of relevant industrial experience, including demonstrated leadership of technical teams; advanced degree preferred.
Proven experience leading ceramic materials, processing, manufacturing development, or scale-up programs in an industrial environment.
Demonstrated ability to manage, coach, and develop engineers, scientists, technicians, or cross-functional technical contributors.
Hands-on familiarity with ceramic processing methods such as extrusion, slip casting, spray coating, isostatic pressing, tape casting, dip coating, gel casting, or related forming and coating processes.
Strong working knowledge of relevant characterization techniques such as dilatometry, rheometry, particle size analysis, SEM, XRD, BET, porosimetry, TGA/DSC, mechanical testing, fractography, or digital image analysis.
Experience applying DOE, statistical methods, root-cause analysis, process qualification, or similar tools to guide technical decisions and process improvement.
Ability to communicate complex technical strategy, risks, and recommendations clearly to executive leadership and technical teams.
Ability to lead effectively in a fast-paced, cross-functional R&D environment with evolving priorities and high ambiguity.

Preferred Qualifications:

MS or PhD in Ceramic Engineering, Materials Science, or a related field.
Prior ownership of a ceramic technology roadmap, platform development program, or multi-year scale-up initiative.
Experience transferring technology from R&D into pilot-scale, internal manufacturing, or third-party manufacturing environments.
Prior experience in aerospace, defense, structural ceramics, refractories, filtration, catalyst supports, thermal management, nuclear materials, or other advanced ceramic manufacturing environments.
Experience establishing technical governance, design review processes, quality gates, or process qualification methods for complex hardware or materials systems.
Familiarity with high-temperature reactor systems, harsh-environment oxide materials, or electrochemical devices.

$200,000 - $250,000 a year

What Will Help Someone Succeed in This Role

A leader who can balance strategic direction with practical engagement in technical details, equipment, data, and team problem-solving.
A disciplined, quantitative mindset that turns ambiguous technical problems into clear priorities, experiments, and decisions.
The ability to build structure without creating bureaucracy, especially in an environment where processes are still being developed, refined, and scaled.
A collaborative leadership style that aligns R&D, manufacturing, external partners, and executive leadership around the highest-impact technical work.

Title: Director Engineering Technical Support

Location: Kennewick, WA

Job Requisition ID: Req-271918

About Lamb Weston

You’ve probably enjoyed our fries without even knowing it! As a leading manufacturer in our industry, we inspire and bring people together with foods they love and trust. Our customer base includes international food service providers, restaurants, and households in over 100 countries around the world.

A highly innovative global corporation with a start-up mindset, we empower every individual to make a genuine difference. You’ll gain access to hands-on training to fuel your growth and success, explore opportunities for new solutions, and you’ll join a winning team of 10,000+ people all dedicated to raising the bar – together.

If you have a strong drive for results, a desire to help us bring the world together through our fries, and are ready for a fresh challenge, we want to hear from you.

Job Description Summary

The Director - Engineering Technical Support shall demonstrate skills in managing Engineering Technical SMEs (Subject Matter Experts). This position requires knowledge of the technical engineering disciplines used in Lamb Weston manufacturing facilities (Electrical, Automation & Controls, Packaging, Boilers & Refrigeration, and Wastewater Treatment) as well as how those technical disciplines support operations and long-term growth.

This position is instrumental in creating asset management plans aimed at maintaining and updating aged technologies and equipment, ensuring proper maintenance, and setting strategies that properly respond to obsolescence, market trends and forces, and internal company initiatives. A major responsibility of this position is to bring the Technical Support team to bear to consult on design for strategic as well as plant projects to assure adherence to standards, promote technical strategic direction, and support execution of projects’ technical areas.

This position also provides leadership and direction for technical SMEs and other engineering disciplines, to develop and execute strategies that improve asset reliability, operational availability, and sustainable plant performance. The Technical Support organization serves as a key partner to plant operations by providing subject matter expertise, standards, troubleshooting support, and long-term reliability improvements that enable safe and reliable manufacturing operations.

This role works hand in hand with other internal business units as well as outside contractors and support groups. Strong interpersonal skills when working with non-technical partners is a must, as is the ability to communicate both horizontally and vertically throughout the organization.

In the area of strategic planning and development, this role directs the Technical Support team to discover, test, and implement new technologies aimed at improving manufacturing processes and efficiencies as well as engaging in ongoing support of existing legacy systems. Consulting, informing, and planning long term strategies in the capital improvement process is a critical function of this position

Job Description

Essential Duties and Responsibilities
include the following. Other duties may be assigned.

Direct management of the Technical Support department teams.
Maintain the necessary levels of technical talent within the department. Prepare and maintain a talent succession plan to ensure business continuity as the workforce ages out and new talent fill positions.
Direct Technical Support SMEs in developing reliability strategies, standards, and technical support processes that improve equipment uptime, reduce operational risk, and ensure reliable plant operations across Electrical, Automation & Controls, Packaging, Utilities, and other critical manufacturing systems
Create and maintain long-term strategic direction for technical areas of responsibility.
Prepare a department budget and be responsible for forecasting and spending within budgeted guidelines.
Take a key role in the annual capital planning activities to develop phased approaches to solve plant technical obsolescence and project challenges.
Serve as primary liaison between the Technical Support group, the I/T organization, and the rest of the Global Engineering team. IT-OT Convergence is an initiative for which this position plays a key role.

Essential Skills

Visionary Leadership - Displays vision and inspiration to engender respect and trust and motivate others to fulfill the company’s vision. Exhibits confidence in self and others and leads to create a culture in which trust, individual purpose, and team building are core tenants.
Oral Communication - Speaks clearly and persuasively.
Written Communication - Writes clearly and informatively with the ability to vary writing style to match the audience.
Presentation – Ability to present effectively to all levels of the organization. Must be able to present technical concepts to non-technical audiences.
Judgment - Displays willingness to make decisions and exhibits sound and accurate judgment. Supports and explains reasoning for decisions and includes appropriate people and ideas in the decision-making process.
Strategic Planning - Keep abreast of technologies, timing, and adoption strategies. Maintain a running 5-year strategic plan for Technical Engineering disciplines.
Planning/Organizing - Prioritizes and plans work activities and uses time efficiently. Ability to set goals and objectives, organize competing priorities, and develop realistic action plans.

Basic & Preferred Qualifications

Ability to apply common sense understanding to carry out instructions furnished in written, oral, or visual form.

Competent understanding of Instrumentation, PLC’s, SCADA systems and advanced control software such as statistical process control, simulation and modeling is required.

Other Requirements

Passport, valid driver's license, and the ability to meet Lamb Weston’s driving record standards. Ability to travel to various plant and vendor locations as required. Ability for extended travel and time away from home to complete projects at various plant locations-20-25% of the time.

jobs.description:
Job Description

At Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), we are building the next generation of cloud services that power mission-critical workloads for customers around the world. OCI combines the speed, ownership, and innovation of a startup with the scale, reliability, and customer focus of one of the world’s leading technology companies.

Oracle Managed Kubernetes (OMK) is Oracle Cloud Infrastructure's (OCI) enterprise-grade Kubernetes service that provides a managed, scalable, and secure environment to deploy containerized applications. It is built on the open-source Kubernetes engine and designed to simplify operations, improve performance, and provide deep integration with the broader OCI ecosystem.

We are seeking an experienced hands-on senior engineering manager to manage and grow a team of highly talented engineers responsible for designing, building, and operating software systems for OMK. You will own delivery, architecture, reliability, and operational health across multiple software areas while developing strong engineering leaders and technical talent.

The ideal candidate is an experienced engineering leader with a strong background in distributed systems, cloud services, operational platforms, and people leadership. You are comfortable operating in ambiguous, high-scale environments, driving technical strategy, building durable teams, and partnering across engineering, product, operations, and infrastructure organizations to deliver measurable business impact.

This is an opportunity to lead teams building software that directly improves how OCI supports global data center infrastructure, reduces operational friction, increases automation, and enables OCI to scale efficiently.

Responsibilities

Key Responsibilities

Platform Software Development:

Lead multiple platform teams to standardize middleware patterns and client libraries used by several consumer teams.
Establish group-level guardrails for APIs/SDKs, deprecation strategies, and upgrade playbooks; track adoption and risk.
Sponsor shared observability frameworks and capacity models across teams; review error-budget posture and corrective actions.

Software Development and Coding - Design, Testing, and Optimization:

Leads teams and provides technical recommendations and guidance in designing software solutions and identifying, analyzing and ensuring alignment with requirements.
Manages the execution of processes to develop and guide new software features and enhancements following design specifications, ensuring accessibility, and to develop documents to clarify software design and code.
Leads code and/or functional reviews to drive improvements across a project.
Leads and reviews teams to conduct debugging and troubleshooting to identify and fix software issues across multiple components or functional areas.
Provides teams guidance to implement software testing (e.g., functional and non-functional), quality assurance processes, software error logging, monitoring, and observability for effective debugging.
Utilizes an analytic approach to conduct performance profiling and optimization of coding.
Leads teams in troubleshooting and resolving issues related to application programming interface (API) functionality and integration.
Leads teams to implement API versioning, lifecycle, and interoperability strategies.

Software Architecture - Software System Structural Design:

Leads teams to design and develop software, systems, and services.
Acts as a role model to provide technical guidance and domain expertise in software architecture decisions and best practices.
Leads teams to conduct periodic reviews and ensures adherence to architectural framework(s) and internal development practices and standards.
Collaborates with cross-functional teams to align and build software architecture with business and/or customer goals and priorities in focus.
Leads teams to implement performance optimization and scalability strategies in software design.
Impacts teams to conduct regular technology research and evaluation for architectural enhancements.

Issue/Defect Collaboration - Software Products Support:

Collaborates with stakeholders and external clients and/or partners to understand customer issues and align solutions.
Leads team(s) to provide technical guidance and appropriately prioritize support to customers regarding reported issues.
Acts as a role model for teams to advocate for customers' interests and suggests product enhancements based on feedback.
Develops, modifies, and executes policies to ensure customer satisfaction through timely resolution of issues and effective communication.
Leads teams through processes for handling customer issues and/or defects handling and directs them to training opportunities as needed.
Manages the investigation and troubleshooting of complex product maintenance issues to ensure customer agreement on short- and long-term solutions.

Practices and Standards Compliance - Security and Compliance:

Collaborates with teams and other stakeholders within and outside of group to establish, follow, and enforce documented security criteria, development industry best practices and processes, and coding standards.
Ensures clarity of teams' operational objectives for adherence to broad acceptance criteria.
Implements moderately complex secure software development practices requiring information gathering and analysis to prevent security vulnerabilities.

Development Operations - System Maintenance:

Leads teams in performing periodic maintenance and testing operations for systems that require upgrading or patching (e.g., for critical vulnerabilities).
Delegates assignments to teams to implement and evolve standard operating procedures (SOP) for development and for driving improvements, ensuring automation, testing, and debugging of systems to ensure service/product availability, health, support, and reliability.

Core Responsibilities

Planning & Execution:

Manages multiple medium- to large-scale projects or initiatives across teams, ensuring timelines, deliverables, and budgets when applicable are monitored and met. Provides direction to teams on project work, setting priorities, and aligning with business needs. Guides teams on adjusting plans to accommodate resource or timeline changes.

Collaboration & Partnership:

Drives cross-functional partnerships to align expectations and shared objectives across multiple teams. Coaches team members to develop strategic relationships with business leaders, stakeholders, and external partners to foster collaboration and long-term success. Promotes inclusivity by actively seeking and listening to diverse perspectives, ensuring others feel heard and respected.

Problem Solving:

Provides direction to multiple teams on addressing complex operational and/or technical issues as well as providing guidance on analyzing complex data and/or information to identify solutions. Reviews and provides insights into unresolved or critical issues, helping the team to identify potential solutions.

Continuous Learning:

Models engaging in continuous learning to deepen expertise and stay ahead of industry trends, integrating best practices into strategic planning. Leverages feedback to drive personal and team skill improvements. Identifies skill gaps across teams, and empowers team members to pursue learning and knowledge sharing opportunities that build their expertise in new areas and coaches them to apply learnings to advance the organization.

Continuous Improvement:

Drives team to collaborate on, develop, and implement ideas to increase the efficiency and effectiveness of processes, protocols, and workflows within and across teams, providing oversight. Guides team to adopt new ideas for alternative approaches and methods and encourages feedback for continued improvement.

Performance and Development:

Drives performance across teams by providing feedback and coaching in alignment with performance management processes, guidelines, and expectations. Discusses development goals with team members, shares opportunities to facilitate career development, and ensures individual goals are aligned with broader organizational goals. Develops and manages talent acquisition pipeline by leading candidate interviews, monitoring promotion eligibility, and/or orchestrating talent resources.

Qualifications

jobs.description:
Description

Senior Manager of Software Engineering

Location:
Wallick Corporate Office – New Albany, OH

Job Type:
Full-time

Make a Difference—And Own Your Future

Join Wallick Communities, a 100% employee-owned company with over 55 years of experience in providing affordable housing and assisted living for families and seniors across the Midwest. With 1,000+ associates and a mission to open doors to homes, opportunity, and hope, we take pride in fostering a supportive and collaborative work environment where every employee-owner plays a vital role.

A Career with Wallick Means. . .

Creating Homes for People Who Need It Most: Providing new beginnings for residents seeking affordable, safe and high-quality housing where they can thrive.
Pay-on-Demand: access your money as you earn it.
Exceptional Benefit Package: Health, dental, vision insurance effective within 2 weeks of starting your new job, paid time off, gym membership reimbursement, paid parental leave, 401K, and more!
Work-Life Balance: Paid time off, including paid parental leave.
Learning & Support: A supportive team that cares about your continued development, well-being and professional growth.
Resident Stories That Stay with You: From Henry, who moved into his first-ever home, to Jaci, whose stay at a Wallick community allowed her to achieve homeownership and graduate college, kickstarting her dream career.
Work-Life Balance: Paid time off, including paid parental leave.
Career Growth: Tuition reimbursement, training, professional development, and advancement opportunities within a company that invests in its people.
Employee Owned, Resident Focused: As a 100% employee-owned company, your daily work (supporting our residents) also contributes to your financial future by sharing in our profitability.

What You’ll Do

The Sr Manager Software Engineering leads Build & Automate, Pillar 2 of Wallick's IT operating model, and holds accountability for every decision within it. The pillar owns the automation portfolio, the integration estate that moves operational data across Yardi, Dayforce, Procore, enterprise systems, and the satellite solutions that extend the systems of record, and it holds Wallick's AI agenda as a joint accountability with the Data & Analytics team. The pillar exists so that Wallick can grow without adding people at the same rate: it automates repetitive work, connects the systems so data moves without being rekeyed, and gives business teams controlled tools for configuration and workflow instead of unrestricted direct admin access to the core systems. You will report to the VP of Information Technology and work together with other team members and leaders.
The seat is deliberately a business-technology leader, not a Principal Architect. The role owns outcomes, priorities, and the pillar's accountability. Deep technical authority lives with the Principal Software Engineer — Integrate & Aggregate, the Sr. manager's trusted technical advisor on architecture and engineering calls. The Leader consults the Principal before committing externally, then decides. Both know the seams, and the model works because they are honest.

What We’re Looking For

Bachelor's degree in business, information systems, computer science, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
A track record, typically built over eight or more years, in delivering business technology solutions, including at least three years leading a technical team or a portfolio of technical work.
Business acumen and stakeholder engagement: able to represent the pillar at the executive table, negotiate priorities with business leaders, and explain a technical trade-off in business terms.
Portfolio and priority judgment: experience running a backlog of integration, automation, and software work against business outcomes, and holding the line on scope.
Growing technical breadth rather than depth: working literacy in integration patterns, workflow automation, AI and agent tooling, and modern application platforms, with the appetite to keep learning and the comfort to decide with strong technical input from a peer whose judgment you trust.
AI and automation strategic literacy, exercised jointly with the Data & Analytics team: able to see where automation and AI change an operating process and where they do not, and to reach those judgments with a peer rather than alone.
Governance experience: solution architecture approval, change and release management, and application portfolio decisions (rationalization, sunset, and portfolio health).
People leadership: developing engineers at different career stages, including a principal-level advisor and an early-career builder.
Familiarity with the Microsoft cloud ecosystem (Microsoft 365, Azure, Power Platform, Copilot Studio) is strongly preferred. Experience in multifamily housing, senior living, or another regulated operating business is a plus.

Functions And Responsibilities

Pillar Leadership and Portfolio Management

Lead the Build & Automate pillar and its portfolio of integration, automation, AI, and software engineering initiatives, aligned with business roadmaps.
Provide leadership and career development for the Principal Software Engineer, Integrate & Aggregate, and the Software Engineer, Extend.
Partner with the Principal Software Engineer on architecture and technical strategy, leveraging the role’s technical expertise before making external commitments.
Represent the pillar with IT leadership and business stakeholders, coordinating cross-pillar priorities with the Leaders of Business Capabilities and IT Operations & Trust.

Integration, Automation, and AI

Own the strategy, priorities, health, and outcomes of enterprise integrations, including data movement across Yardi, Dayforce, Procore, and other systems, as well as modernization of legacy integrations.
Oversee the integrations and pipelines that deliver operational data to the Data & Analytics platform, in coordination with business data owners, Data & Analytics, and Power & Protect.
Jointly lead the automation and AI portfolio with Data & Analytics, including prioritization, governance, delivery, and measurement of business value.
Co-chair the AI Council, which governs AI policy, platforms, licensing, data access, investment priorities, and value measurement. Escalate unresolved decisions to the SVP of Organizational Effectiveness and Technology.
Move validated concepts from experimentation into scalable, supported enterprise solutions.

Architecture, Governance, and Applications

Own solution architecture for the pillar, with the Principal Software Engineer developing technical patterns and standards for leadership review and approval.
Oversee change and release governance for pillar solutions.
Manage the application portfolio, including the application register, portfolio health, rationalization, and retirement decisions. Commercial license management remains with the Vendor Management Analyst.
Chair the weekly cross-pillar technical council to coordinate standards, dependencies, and technical decisions.

Transformation Program Leadership

Serve as the default leader for major cross-pillar transformation programs with a significant technology build component, subject to assignment by the VP of Information Technology.
Deliver programs with clear scope, priorities, dependencies, and sequencing.
Partner with Partner & Transform from program inception to incorporate stakeholder engagement, change management, and adoption into delivery plans.

Wallick’s Mission & Values

At Wallick Communities, We Believe In Opening Doors To Homes, Opportunity, And Hope For Our Residents, Associates, And Community. Our Core Values Guide Everything We Do

Care – We show compassion and respect for everyone.
Character – We do the right thing, even when no one is looking.
Collaboration – We work together to achieve more.

At Wallick, we celebrate Diversity, Equity, Inclusion + Belonging (DEI+B) in our workplace and communities, creating an environment where associates feel welcome, respected, and empowered to bring their authentic selves to the great work they do every day.

For nearly 60 years, it has been at the core of our organization’s culture that all Wallick associates come to a safe and inclusive place to work. Wallick does not discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, gender identity, and sexual orientation), parental status, national origin, age, disability, genetic information (including family medical history), political affiliation, military service, or other non-merit-based factors.

If you're ready to make a difference in people’s lives while securing your financial future, apply today!

Hands-on experience leading a Generative AI and AI Agents

SitelogIQ
is a world-class team making a large-scale impact on the efficiency and sustainability of the places we live, work, shop, and heal.

SitelogIQ delivers turnkey solutions across energy efficiency: lighting upgrades
, EV infrastructure
, solar and energy storage system
[distributed generation (DG)] , and other facility improvement measures (FIMs)
that transform built environments and breathe life into the sustainability, financial, and resiliency goals of real estate teams, corporations and public sector organizations across the U.S. Our mission is to make buildings better while making it easy for our clients to accelerate their impact.

Job Summary

The Director of Engineering & Development for Distributed Generation
within our Commercial Markets Division
provides strategic leadership and oversight of the project engineering and development function and team. This role establishes departmental priorities and standards across team management, tools and systems, project scope development, engineering execution, budget estimating, scheduling, quality, risk management, and workflow.

Key Components Of This Role Include

Management: Strategic leadership and management of the DG team, including Project Development Engineers; oversight of resource planning, project priorities, workflows, day-to-day operations, training and mentoring, performance, and continuous improvement.
Project Engineering & Development: Direct, facilitate, and/or review site survey [audit] analysis, conceptual project designs, estimating, schedules, product specifications, code research and application, and the preparation of proposal documents.

An effective SitelogIQ Director of Engineering & Development will partner with leaders across Sales, Operations, and Project Management and represent the team and its technical solutions to clients and their technical staff. They will oversee program and project development milestones to deliver timely, comprehensive proposals that clearly communicate project intentions and solutions while meeting SitelogIQ financial and risk metrics. SitelogIQ team members are expected to share knowledge with others by serving as a constant contributor, trainer, mentor, and resource.

$145,000 - $180,000 dependent on experience.

Director, Engineering & Development Responsibilities

Provide leadership, direction, coaching, and mentorship to the team as they develop and produce DG project designs and proposals.
Oversee the internal proposal queue, resource allocation, team assignments, risk review process, and client commitments.
Facilitate collaboration between the Engineering & Development and Sales teams to determine customers’ specific technical requirements, project scope, definition of work, and product feature needs.

Lead the development of new processes, tools, and workflows and the continuous improvement of existing practices.

Review and present DG solution proposals

Any, and all ad hoc reporting, requests or other tasks deemed
