jobs.title: VP of Engineering
jobs.description:
Our Mission and Vision

Unlearn exists to transform clinical development by making every trial smarter. We harness data, AI, and digital twins to enable faster, more robust studies that bring life-saving treatments to patients faster. This mission drives everything we do as we partner with biopharmaceutical companies to redesign how clinical trials are planned, run, and analyzed.

We are defining the future of clinical development with unmatched scientific credibility, replacing uncertainty with AI-powered precision so decisions are clearer and trials are stronger. We don’t just disrupt the pharmaceutical industry, we create lasting change.

We believe AI will define the future of medicine, and we are committed to building that future responsibly, rigorously, and in close collaboration with our partners in clinical development.

About Our Team

We come from a variety of backgrounds ranging from machine learning to marketing—but regardless of where we come from, Unlearners share some common traits:

Unlearners are ambitious; we aren’t intimidated by big, challenging goals.
Unlearners are disciplined experimenters; we break down our big goals into smaller chunks and meet as often as necessary to track our velocity and iterate quickly.
Unlearners are gritty; we never give up, setbacks just make us try harder.
Unlearners are receptive to new ideas; in fact, we hate being stuck with the status quo
Unlearners are storytellers; sharing information with each other and with the world is super important, too important to be boring. And, last but not least,
Unlearners are team-oriented; we put the mission first, the company second, the team third, and individuals last.

Headquartered in San Francisco, Unlearn was founded in 2017 by a team of world-class machine learning scientists. We have raised venture capital from top tier investors such as Altimeter, Insight Partners, Radical Ventures, 8VC, DCVC, and DCVC Bio, and completed our $50 million Series C in January 2024.

If our purpose and culture resonate with you, we invite you to apply.

Your Role

Leading Pharma and Biotech companies trust Unlearn to deliver scientifically rigorous work using digital twins on studies where the stakes are high and the timelines are real. A digital twin of a patient is a comprehensive prediction of expected outcomes under a defined standard of care, made by a machine learning model built using our proprietary technology. Working at scale across the industry requires a strong engineering foundation built around data, models, and AI in a regulated, compliance-heavy environment.

As the VP of Engineering, you will lead our engineering function, an organization of engineers spanning core engineering, applications, ML/AI Ops, and infrastructure. The team includes engineers across experience levels, anchored by strong senior technical leaders. Engineering plays a critical role in our ability to deliver AI technology through models, applications, and agentic systems, and this role will ensure the potential of AI systems are realized across that technical stack.

This is an execution-focused leadership role, focused on the core engineering systems, software applications, infrastructure, and forward deployment that drive AI-heavy, tech-enabled services. You will work with your teams on scoping and delivery, and lead an engineering organization known for shipping what it commits to. You will partner closely with Product, Delivery, and R&D teams to understand requirements, integrate engineering with our customer delivery teams, and build the platform and tools they use to do their best work.

Just as importantly, you will connect engineering to the company's direction, understanding company strategy, translating it into a concrete engineering roadmap that integrates a workflow across data, modeling, applications, compliance, and security, and holding the team accountable for delivering to that roadmap on timeframes that match company objectives. You will work as a member of the leadership team, maintaining consistent communication and clear expectations in both directions, so that leadership always knows where engineering stands, and engineering always knows why its work matters.

Responsibilities

Lead Unlearn's engineering function across technical disciplines, owning the quality, reliability, compliance, and security of the systems that power our work. Ensure AI tools and systems are used heavily for efficiency and impact.

Build the software operating layer for autonomous mobility

San Francisco Bay Area, CA

Location:
Downtown San Francisco / Bay Area — in person when required

Full-Time

Autonomous Mobility | Fleet Software | AI Infrastructure | EV & AV Operations

About Autzu

Autzu is building the software and operational layer that autonomous mobility will run on.
Over the past several years, Autzu has developed and operated technology supporting live electric-vehicle fleets across the U.S. and Canada. We are now evolving that experience into an autonomous-ready platform capable of deploying, monitoring, coordinating, and managing vehicles across multiple operators, vehicle platforms, and markets.
Our mission is to make autonomous fleets commercially deployable at scale.
Autzu will own the software layer connecting:
Autonomous vehicles and fleet operators
Vehicle state, telemetry, diagnostics, and readiness
Dispatch, scheduling, charging, maintenance, and service workflows
Remote operations and human-in-the-loop support
Data infrastructure, operational intelligence, and AI-driven automation
Future autonomous hubs and robotic servicing systems

We are not building another autonomous-driving stack. We are building the platform that allows different autonomous systems to operate reliably across real-world fleets and markets.
Autzu will also work directly with Infra
, a separately structured robotics-infrastructure company focused on physical autonomous hubs and robotic servicing systems. Autzu’s platform will provide the software, data, orchestration, and integration layer connecting autonomous vehicles with Infra’s physical infrastructure.
The Opportunity

We are seeking a hands-on, execution-focused Head of Engineering
to lead Autzu’s software organization through its next stage of development.
This is a founding engineering leadership seat for Autzu’s autonomous-systems platform.
The role is not focused on building robotic arms or developing an autonomous-driving stack. It is focused on building the software platform that connects vehicles, operators, partners, operational teams, and future robotic infrastructure.
You will own and strengthen Autzu’s existing fleet platform while architecting its evolution into a secure, scalable, multi-operator autonomous fleet orchestration system.
You must be comfortable maintaining live production software while modernizing the architecture and developing new autonomous-vehicle capabilities in parallel.
You Will

Own and strengthen Autzu’s existing fleet and operations platform.
Define the architecture and technical roadmap for Autzu’s autonomous fleet platform.
Build an agnostic integration layer capable of supporting multiple autonomous-vehicle operators, OEMs, and technology stacks.
Lead the development of vehicle-state, telemetry, diagnostics, readiness, dispatch, and operational workflow systems.
Develop the software interfaces connecting Autzu’s platform with Infra’s future robotics and autonomous-hub infrastructure.
Improve platform reliability, data integrity, security, and system observability.
Reduce technical debt without disrupting live operations.
Hire and lead a lean, senior engineering team across backend systems, autonomous systems, data, AI, and edge or IoT integration.
Work directly with Autzu’s founder, executive team, board, customers, and strategic technology partners.
Represent Autzu’s technical architecture and product direction in partner, investor, and fundraising conversations.

Core Mandate

Keep Autzu’s current fleet software operating reliably while transforming it into a modular, secure, autonomous-ready platform capable of coordinating vehicles and operations across multiple cities, countries, vehicle types, and autonomy providers.
This includes:
Stabilizing uptime, data quality, and operational reliability.
Introducing clear service boundaries, APIs, and data contracts without a disruptive rewrite.
Creating a common vehicle and fleet data model across multiple platforms.
Building real-time vehicle-state, telemetry, diagnostics, and exception-management systems.
Developing integration frameworks for AV operators, OEMs, mobility platforms, telematics providers, charging networks, and maintenance partners.
Establishing a software interface between Autzu’s fleet platform and Infra’s robotic hub systems.
Strengthening CI/CD, automated testing, release management, incident response, audit logging, and on-call processes.
Building the migration path from today’s fleet platform into a multi-city autonomous operations layer.
Introducing AI agents and automation where they improve reliability, efficiency, and operational decision-making.

What You’ll Do

Define and own Autzu’s engineering vision and roadmap alongside the founder and executive team.
Lead backend, cloud, data, platform, and selected edge or embedded-software functions.
Make key architecture decisions while remaining close enough to the implementation to review designs, challenge assumptions, and guide senior engineers.
Build systems for vehicle onboarding, state management, fleet readiness, dispatch, monitoring, diagnostics, and operational workflows.
Develop real-time APIs and event-driven integrations across autonomous vehicles, fleet operators, and external services.
Build the systems needed for remote supervision, exception handling, human intervention, and operational escalation.
Oversee integrations with marketplace APIs, payments, telematics, charging networks, maintenance providers, identity systems, and compliance reporting.
Develop data and AI systems that identify operational issues, automate repetitive workflows, and improve fleet utilization.
Establish engineering standards across architecture, code quality, testing, security, observability, and release management.
Manage existing contractors while recruiting and developing key internal engineering leaders.
Create a builder culture grounded in accountability, speed, technical rigor, and measurable operational outcomes.

Must-Have Experience

8+ years of software or systems engineering experience.
4+ years in engineering leadership as a Head of Engineering, Director, VP Engineering, CTO, Engineering Manager, or comparable technical leader.
Proven ownership of a live production software platform supporting operationally critical workflows.
Experience building distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, APIs, data pipelines, and complex third-party integrations.
Demonstrated ability to modernize architecture and reduce technical debt while continuing to ship new capabilities.
Strong operational discipline around uptime, observability, incident response, release cycles, security, and data integrity.
Experience hiring and leading strong engineers in a fast-moving or resource-constrained environment.
Ability to translate business and operational requirements into scalable technical systems.
Comfortable working directly with external technical partners, customers, executives, and investors.
Hands-on enough to lead architecture reviews, evaluate code and system design, and guide Staff or Principal-level engineers.

Strongly Preferred

Experience in autonomous vehicles, robotics software, mobility, rideshare, logistics, fleet management, connected vehicles, or intelligent transportation.
Experience with fleet orchestration, remote operations, vehicle telemetry, diagnostics, mapping, calibration, simulation, or autonomous-system infrastructure.
Familiarity with edge computing, embedded systems, IoT, telematics, CAN or vehicle interfaces.
Experience integrating software platforms with physical hardware or robotics systems.
Familiarity with NVIDIA’s automotive, edge-computing, simulation, or Physical AI ecosystem.
Experience building AI agents, operational automation, predictive systems, or intelligent decision-support tools.
Experience with safety-critical, regulated, or compliance-heavy environments.
Experience scaling software platforms across multiple cities, countries, or operating partners.

What We Offer

A founding engineering leadership role in Autzu’s transition into autonomous fleet operations.
Significant ownership over the engineering strategy, architecture, team, and technical roadmap.
Competitive compensation, performance incentives, and meaningful equity.
A dedicated budget to build a lean, high-caliber engineering organization.
Direct partnership with the founder, executive team, board, and strategic technology partners.
The opportunity to build the software platform connecting autonomous vehicles, fleet operations, and future robotic infrastructure.
A direct working relationship with Infra as its physical robotics and autonomous-hub systems are developed.
The opportunity to grow into broader technology leadership as Autzu’s platform, team, and international operations scale.

Why This Role Matters

Autonomous vehicles cannot scale through driving technology alone.
They require software that understands where every vehicle is, what condition it is in, what it needs next, when human intervention is required, and how it moves through charging, maintenance, service, and deployment workflows.
Autzu is building that operating layer.
The Head of Engineering will be responsible for turning that vision into a reliable production platform.

Congratulations on taking the first step toward embarking on an exciting new adventure at Barclays Center! Our focus is YOU!

jobs.title: VP / Director of Engineering
jobs.description:
Who We Are

Expand Power is building solid-state transformers and modular power electronics for a decentralized, decentralized, resilient grid. We're a small team doing hard, meaningful engineering, and we're just getting started.

We’re backed by several Department of Energy programs, Berkeley National Laboratory, the Activate Fellowship, and world-class pre-seed investors and VCs. Our advisory network includes prominent leaders in power electronics, high frequency magnetics, the electric utility industry, and deep tech commercialization.

Why This Role Exists

We’re at a critical inflection point in the grid, where we have new sources and loads at a capacity that we couldn’t have dreamed of. Traditional grid electronics, with their lack of control and DC based capabilities, just can’t keep up. With real customer demand, we’re closing the gap between the grid of today and the grid of the future by building innovative smart transformers and modular power electronics. We’re excited to commercialize and deploy our technology across multiple customers for real world impact. We are growing the team and are looking for passionate, dedicated, ambitious hires who are excited by ownership and the electrification of our grid.

The Vice President / Director of Engineering will serve as a founding team member and strategic partner to the CEO, leading the architecture of Expand’s technical stack and defining the next generation of power electronics for the grid. As a core member of the founding leadership team, the VP will shape Expand’s technical priorities through immediate pilots and deployment, ensuring customers receive a high performance, reliable, product. 

This role is critical to Expand’s success– you will be working closely with the founding team and in the field with real customers, reporting to the CEO. In this role, you’ll set technical requirements and ensure customer functionality is translated into complex technical goals. You’ll be deeply hands-on and in the weeds while also leading the technology roadmap and progress. You will guide technical development of our proprietary power electronics technology for immediate deployment while interfacing with customers. You will have a critical role in shaping the core technology, product direction, and culture of a cross-functional and rapidly growing early stage company. You’ll be one of the most valuable founding members of a company shaping the future of the electric grid. In doing so, you will push the limits of what’s achievable with high-frequency power electronics and grid modernization

Your Day to Day and Key Responsibilities

You will be leading Expand’s technical strategy from customer discussions to prototype to certifications to manufacturing while guiding the engineering team and contributing to technical designs. You’ll use creativity and innovation to:

Leadership
Leverage deep expertise in power electronics to understand complex customer needs, set and lead the technical roadmap, and execute while adhering to regulatory requirements
Lead the development and evolution of Expand’s technical stack, aligning customer demand, industry trends, and operational capabilities in direct partnership with the CEO
Act as the technical point of contact for customers, translating requirements into engineering tasks
Define and oversee operational excellence for Expand’s technical spaces, ensuring a safe, high-quality, and consistent user experience
Lead and scale the technical team, fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement
Support business development efforts to bring new customers
Provide strategic technical insight to inform Expand’s broader growth, partnership, and capital planning decisions
Architect the technical narratives for capital formation efforts alongside the CEO, including input for grants, funding, and early commercial partnerships
Contribute as a core member of the founding team to define and institutionalize Expand’s mission, values, safety standards, and internal operating systems
Represent Expand in select industry, government, and customer-facing forums
Maintain alignment of technical standards and customer experience
Partner with the CEO to forecast hiring needs aligned with customer demand and program growth

Hands on Engineering
Lead the development of power conversion systems from first principles to deployment for manufacturability and flexibility 
Document technical specifications, architecture decisions, and validation reports
Lead IP generation process
Simulate, model, and design circuits and converters to maximize performance and reliability, as needed

What You’ve Done

Required Experience
You have deep power electronics expertise, with a proven ability to scale a product from inception to manufacturing while building a powerful team. You’ve done this before: you are a highly experienced electrical engineering leader, a master of your craft. Guiding hardware development is your bread and butter, but it still gives you excitement and fulfillment, especially with a mission you care deeply about. You have a proven track record of driving and implementing innovation and R&D for commercialization. 

You also have experience in
Leadership in power electronics and hardware design with demonstrated experience advancing new technologies and products toward manufacturing 
Building multi-disciplinary power electronics teams
Architecting multi-year technical roadmaps aligned with commercialization timelines, customer demand, and operational capabilities in a founding-stage, high-growth, or innovation-driven organization
Bringing a product to market while meeting certification standards and regulations
Technical consulting or customer-facing roles, with the ability to translate ambiguous research goals into precise commercialization steps
Strong relationship building and communication skills, with the ability to build trust across technical teams, customers, and senior stakeholders ranging from academic researchers to industry experts
Startups or fast-paced, early stage company environments
High frequency and high power converters, including modular multilevel converters, resonant converters, or MVDC distribution
Fluency in Altium and/or KiCad, ANSYS, Spice, PLECS, PSIM

Bonus Experience
Medium voltage power electronics and operation
Planar magnetics
DERs and/or inverter product development
Knowledge of relevant industry standards (UL 1741, etc)
Overseeing or operating technical laboratory, prototyping, or shared infrastructure environments with rigorous attention to safety (EH&S), resource allocation, and operational efficiency

You’re described as a
Fast moving, hands-on builder, taking responsibility for outcomes from design through deployment and hungry for ownership
Independent, gritty problem solver, who thrives in uncertainty, loves a challenge, and responds to obstacles with the best of their abilities
Strong and collaborative communicator, able to explain technical decisions to both engineers and non-technical stakeholders, and to share feedback openly and kindly
Mission-driven, motivated by positive real-world impact and passionate about pushing the boundaries of power electronics and electrification
Fearless and endlessly curious, energized by open questions and new possibilities, willing to bet on bold ideas and learn fast from what the hardware tells you, and taking intelligent risks with a sense of wonder and a drive to explore what's possible

Don't meet every requirement? Apply anyway—we value diverse backgrounds and potential over perfect checklists. We're more interested in what you can do than in every box being ticked.

How We Work & Compensation

Come work on breakthrough technology in a collaborative, mission-driven culture with direct influence over company trajectory and room to grow as the team scales. This is an onsite position based in the San Francisco Bay Area. Minimum travel will be expected. We are open to supporting relocation for the right candidate.

We want you to stay for a while– you will receive $175,000 - $225,000 base with meaningful early employee equity, based on level and experience, as well as benefits:
Health Insurance: We offer 100% coverage of employee premiums

jobs.description:
Profluent is the frontier AI lab for biology. Profluent builds powerful foundation models for all of life's molecules, unlocking solutions that transform medicine, agriculture, and beyond. Founded in 2022 and headquartered in Emeryville, CA, Profluent is backed by leading investors including Altimeter Capital, Bezos Expeditions, Spark Capital, Insight Partners, Air Street Capital, AIX Ventures, and Convergent Ventures and has raised over $150M to date.

We're looking for a Director of Software and Data Engineering to lead Profluent's software engineering function and build the platform connecting AI-driven protein design, high-throughput experimental screening, and quantitative data analysis.

You'll own the software and data architecture connecting computational designs to the constructs, samples, assays, and measurements generated through automated laboratory workflows. Your team will build the scientist-facing tools, integrations, and data systems needed to manage experimental data at scale, preserve lineage and context, and turn results into reliable inputs for analysis, machine learning, and the next round of design.

The ideal candidate is an experienced engineering leader with a strong technical foundation, sound judgment, and a track record of building scalable data platforms. You'll manage and mentor a small team while remaining close to architecture, data modeling, and technical decision-making, partnering across science, automation, data, and ML to advance Profluent's lab-in-the-loop platform.

Responsibilities

Lead, mentor, and grow Profluent's software engineering team, with responsibility for technical direction, hiring, organizational development, and execution
Own the roadmap for software and data engineering, balancing scientific impact, user needs, delivery speed, scalability, and long-term platform strategy
Define the software and data architecture, system boundaries, and data flows connecting computational design, high-throughput experimentation, analysis, and machine learning
Architect and guide delivery of scientist-facing applications and data systems supporting experimental design, sample tracking, laboratory automation, assay data capture, and analysis
Establish scalable data models and standards for identifiers, provenance, lineage, versioning, interoperability, and access control, ensuring experimental results are reliable, reusable, and model-ready
Partner across science, automation, bioinformatics, data science, and ML while establishing strong engineering and product practices that drive reliable delivery and adoption

Qualifications

8+ years of software engineering experience, including 3+ years managing or leading engineers
BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, Bioengineering, Computational Biology, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience
Track record of leading teams that architect and deliver production-quality, data-intensive software platforms
Strong technical foundation in Python, backend systems, databases, APIs, cloud infrastructure, and modern software development practices
Experience designing data architectures, schemas, and domain models for complex scientific, experimental, or similarly interconnected workflows
Demonstrated ability to translate ambiguous user and scientific needs into reliable systems, make sound technical and product tradeoffs, and drive adoption

Preferences

Experience building scientific data infrastructure, research software, LIMS integrations, or scientist-facing applications
Experience with Benchling, laboratory automation, instrument integration, sample tracking, or high-throughput experimental platforms
Experience connecting experimental workflows with downstream analysis and machine learning
Familiarity with biological data from protein engineering, gene editing, sequencing, screening, or mammalian or bacterial systems
Frontend development experience and an interest in building intuitive scientist-facing interfaces

What We Offer

High-growth opportunity with meaningful impact on the future of protein design
Competitive compensation package with equity participation
401(k) with a strong employer match
Comprehensive benefits including health/dental/vision insurance
Generous PTO policy and commitment to work-life balance
Professional development opportunities in a cutting-edge field at the intersection of AI and biology

jobs.description:
VERRA MOBILITY

SOFTWARE ENGINEERING

Director, Software Engineering

Who we are...

Verra Mobility is a global leader in smart mobility. We develop technology-enabled solutions that help the world move safely and easily. We are fostering the development of safe cities, working with police departments and municipalities to install over 4,000 red-light, speed, and school bus stop arm safety cameras across North America. We are also creating smart roadways, serving the world's largest commercial fleets and rental car companies to manage tolling transactions and violations for over 8.5 million vehicles. And we are a leading provider of connected systems, processing nearly 165 million transactions each year across 50+ individual tolling authorities.

Culture

Verra Mobility Corporation is a dynamic, entrepreneurial company that operates with a people-first philosophy and approach. The company lives by its core values—Do What's Right, Choose Courage Over Comfort, Win Together, and Own It—in everything it does for its customers and team members. The company seeks to grow, both organically and through acquisition, to continue to be the undisputed market leader with a bias for action, customer focus, teamwork, drive for results, and commitment to excellence.

Position Overview

The Director, Software Engineering is the technical subject matter expert and engineering leader for the Platform portfolio, reporting to the SVP, Software Engineering and owning technology strategy and end to end delivery outcomes for the portfolio's squads. This role requires deep domain expertise in the portfolio's problem space, current fluency across modern engineering practices, and the operating pace expected of a modern software organization.

You will partner with the external Product Portfolio Director on product vision, engage directly with partner and customer technical teams on architecture and integration, and be responsible for evaluating and developing the technical leadership within your portfolio. Your work will determine how quickly a steady state organization can move, and whether the portfolio's platforms are built once and reused, or rebuilt every time a new need arises.

Essential Responsibilities

Technical Strategy & Architecture

Own Portfolio Technology Strategy:
Define technology strategy and end to end delivery outcomes for the portfolio's squads, maintaining deep domain expertise in the portfolio's problem space and current fluency in the broader technology and competitive landscape, including modern AI and machine learning solution categories.
Identify Reuse Before Rebuild:
Identify where shared platform capabilities can be extended or reused rather than rebuilt, partnering with the Platform team and Senior Enterprise Architect to avoid duplicated effort.
Maintain Domain and Integration Fluency:
Maintain a working view of service boundaries, API contracts, and event driven or asynchronous processing patterns across the portfolio, recognizing a fragile integration or a duplicative build before it hardens into a dependency other teams must unwind.

Delivery, Migration & Operational Ownership

Own End to End Delivery:
Own predictable, high quality delivery across the portfolio's squads, including roadmap commitments, release readiness, budget adherence, and operational stability.
Raise Delivery Pace:
Change how quickly a steady state organization moves, accelerating delivery pace and urgency within an existing, already staffed organization.
Lead Platform Migrations:
Lead live system migrations and legacy platform transitions, including cutover sequencing, data reconciliation, and rollback planning, as clients and workloads move off legacy platforms and onto current ones.
Govern Data & Security:
Apply data architecture and governance principles, including data lineage and stewardship for shared or regulated datasets, and ensure the portfolio's systems meet security and compliance expectations for multi tenant, transaction heavy systems operating across multiple jurisdictions.
Own Bid & Contract Review:
Own final review and approval of new contracts and bids for the Platform portfolio, building on the Manager's initial technical and compliance review to confirm proposed work is achievable within existing governance, architectural, and delivery constraints before commitments are made.

Talent & Organizational Leadership

Develop Technical Leaders:
Personally assess whether direct and indirect reports are functioning above or below the title held, and act on that assessment through coaching, role redefinition, or personnel change.
Ensure Technical Succession:
Treat technical succession as a stated priority, so no portfolio depends on a single person's tenure for its technical continuity.
Partner Across the Enterprise:
Partner closely with the Portfolio Architect as the technical decision making pair for the portfolio, coordinate with peer Directors and the Senior Enterprise Architect to keep cross portfolio integrations coherent, and align regularly with the Product Portfolio Director function to reconcile product vision and technical reality.

We're looking for a technical leader with a proven track record of owning outcomes, modernizing platforms, and raising delivery pace at scale. The ideal candidate will bring the following capabilities:

Portfolio Technology Strategy

Ability to define and sustain a coherent technology strategy across a multi squad portfolio, balancing standardization with legitimate portfolio specific divergence.

Architecture & Integration Judgment

Fluency in domain boundaries, API contract design, and event driven or asynchronous processing patterns, sufficient to judge whether a proposed integration is a durable seam or a future liability.

Migration & Modernization Leadership

Demonstrated experience leading a live system migration or legacy platform transition, including cutover sequencing, data reconciliation, and rollback planning.

Data & Governance Fluency

Working knowledge of data architecture, data lineage, and the security and compliance considerations relevant to multi tenant, transaction heavy systems.

Talent Development & Succession

Track record of assessing, coaching, and developing technical leaders, including making difficult talent calls when needed.

Executive & Partner Communication

Technical credibility sufficient to lead architecture and technology discussions directly with partner and customer engineering teams, and to evaluate a vendor pitch or build proposal critically.

Bid & Contract Ownership

Ability to review and approve contracts and bids for technical, architectural, and delivery feasibility, ensuring commitments are not made against a portfolio that cannot support them.

Qualifications

Experience:
10+ years in software engineering delivering enterprise systems, including 5+ years leading multiple teams or squads through Managers and Tech Leads. Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent experience required.
Technical Fluency:
Current fluency with modern engineering stacks relevant to the portfolio, including .NET/C#, Java, SQL, modern web frameworks, REST and GraphQL APIs, microservices, cloud platforms, and event driven or asynchronous processing patterns such as message queues and event streaming.
Migration & Legacy Transition:
Demonstrated experience leading a live system migration or legacy platform transition, including cutover sequencing, data reconciliation, and rollback planning.
Data & Compliance:
Working knowledge of data architecture and governance principles, including data lineage and stewardship, and fluency in security and compliance considerations for multi tenant, transaction heavy systems operating across multiple jurisdictions.
AI & Emerging Technology:
Working knowledge of current AI and machine learning solution categories and their practical application in transaction heavy, government adjacent, or mobility industries, sufficient to evaluate a vendor pitch or build proposal critically and weigh build versus buy trade offs.
Talent Leadership:
Demonstrated willingness and ability to make difficult talent calls, including role realignment or replacement, along with strong judgment on when to standardize across the enterprise versus allow portfolio specific divergence.
Contract & Bid Review:
Ability to evaluate contracts and bids for technical, architectural, and compliance feasibility, owning final review and approval ahead of executive sign off.
Domain Expertise (Preferred):
Experience in mobility, tolling, parking, or other transaction heavy, government adjacent industries is preferred, along with leading an organization through transformation from steady state maintenance to active platform investment.
Vendor & Partner Evaluation (Preferred):
Experience evaluating or negotiating build versus buy decisions for major platform capabilities, including vendor and partner architecture reviews, and experience partnering with an external product organization on a shared roadmap, is also a plus.

Verra Mobility Values

An ideal candidate for this role naturally works in alignment with the Verra Mobility Core Values:

Own It:
We focus on high performance and drive toward breakthrough outcomes. Our employees ensure accountability, optimize and align work, focus on the customer, and cultivate innovation.
Do What's Right:
We champion integrity and good character. Our team members model ethical behavior, demonstrate good judgment and are courageous.
Choose Courage Over Comfort:
We lean into the conversations, decisions and actions that move the business forward, even when they feel uncomfortable. We challenge assumptions, address issues early and prioritize progress over ease.
Win Together:
We believe in growing and inspiring people together. We seek people who collaborate, value differences, think and act globally, foster an engaging work environment, and recognize and develop others.

Engineering Director

Location: San Antonio, TX
Work Arrangement: Onsite
Salary: $115,000–$125,000 per year
Schedule: Monday–Friday, 7:30 AM–4:00 PM
Hours: 40 hours per week
Weekend Work: Occasional Saturday/Sunday work may be required based on customer availability
Direct Reports: 8

ABOUT US:

We are a well-established industrial automation and engineering company specializing in the design and delivery of custom automation solutions for a wide range of manufacturing and industrial applications
Our multidisciplinary engineering organization brings together expertise across mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, controls, robotics, and automation. We develop technically sound, manufacturable, safe, and commercially viable solutions tailored to each customer's unique production requirements
From concept development and engineering through fabrication, assembly, commissioning, and customer delivery, our teams work collaboratively throughout the full project lifecycle. This provides engineering leaders with the opportunity to make a direct impact on technical execution, operational performance, team development, and customer success

JOB DESCRIPTION:

The Engineering Director
will lead and manage the Engineering Department, providing strategic and technical leadership across mechanical, electrical, controls, robotics, and other engineering disciplines
This role is responsible for ensuring the engineering organization consistently delivers technically sound, manufacturable, safe, and profitable automation solutions
that meet customer requirements, project schedules, budgets, and company standards
The Engineering Director will currently oversee a team of 8 direct reports
and will be responsible for developing the people, processes, standards, technical discipline, and accountability required for successful project execution
The Director is not expected to personally solve every engineering problem. Instead, the role is responsible for ensuring engineering issues are identified, assigned, managed, escalated when necessary, and ultimately resolved

DETAILED RESPONSIBILITIES:

Provide overall leadership and direction across mechanical, electrical, controls, robotics, and other engineering disciplines

Lead, manage, and develop a team of approximately 8 engineering professionals

Establish departmental priorities, allocate resources, resolve conflicts, and maintain accountability across the engineering organization
Ensure engineering milestones are established, monitored, and achieved
Monitor engineering hours, schedules, technical risks, procurement dependencies, and project deliverables
Identify projects at risk of falling behind schedule and initiate corrective action before issues impact fabrication, assembly, commissioning, or customer delivery
Maintain responsibility for the technical integrity of engineering designs
released by the department
Ensure appropriate design reviews are completed for critical systems
Ensure engineering solutions meet customer specifications, applicable standards, safety requirements, and internal engineering practices
Develop and enforce standardized design practices, drawing standards, component selection, programming standards, documentation requirements, BOM practices, revision control, and reusable engineering libraries

Ensure engineering works closely with machining, fabrication, assembly, electrical, and commissioning teams
Promote Design for Manufacturing and Assembly (DFMA)
principles, including manufacturability, assembly efficiency, accessibility, serviceability, cost, and lead time
Maintain visibility of engineering workload across active and upcoming projects
Allocate engineering personnel based on capability, workload, project priority, and technical requirements
Identify staffing, subcontracting, and scheduling constraints before they become project risks
Monitor actual engineering hours against quoted and budgeted hours
Investigate engineering budget overruns, identify root causes, and implement corrective actions
Ensure engineering decisions balance technical performance with commercial responsibility

Develop engineers through coaching, technical mentoring, training, performance reviews, and increasing levels of responsibility
Identify skill gaps and establish employee development plans
Build organizational depth and reduce dependency on individual employees for critical technical knowledge
Establish clear expectations around communication, ownership, schedule performance, documentation, attention to detail, and completion of assigned responsibilities
Address recurring performance issues promptly and appropriately
Maintain strong communication between Engineering, Project Management, Sales, Purchasing, Manufacturing, Assembly, and Service

Ensure engineering proactively communicates technical changes, project risks, delays, and decisions that may affect other departments
Participate in customer technical discussions when appropriate, including concept development, design reviews, specification clarification, FAT preparation, and significant technical issue resolution

Ensure customer changes, scope changes, and internal design changes are properly documented and communicated before significant engineering or manufacturing work proceeds
Support Project Management in identifying changes that may require additional cost or schedule adjustments
Conduct post-project engineering reviews to identify recurring problems, lessons learned, design improvements, standardization opportunities, and opportunities to reduce engineering hours
Identify technical and execution risks early and escalate significant schedule, cost, safety, or performance concerns
to executive management
Stay current with emerging technologies, industry trends, engineering tools, and automation technologies
Identify and implement technologies and processes that improve engineering efficiency, strengthen technical capabilities, and maintain competitiveness within the automation industry
Perform other engineering leadership responsibilities as assigned

MUST-HAVE QUALIFICATIONS:

The successful candidate should have a strong combination of hands-on engineering design experience and engineering management experience

Required qualifications include:

Proven experience leading and managing engineering teams
Strong hands-on background in engineering design
, preferably within industrial automation, custom machinery, manufacturing equipment, or a similar environment
Experience managing multidisciplinary engineering functions
Strong understanding of mechanical, electrical, controls, robotics, and automation engineering disciplines

Proven experience managing engineering resources, schedules, budgets, and project priorities
Strong understanding of design for manufacturing and assembly (DFMA)

Experience establishing and enforcing engineering standards, processes, and documentation practices
Strong technical problem-solving and decision-making skills
Experience managing engineering projects through the full project lifecycle
Experience identifying and managing technical, schedule, cost, and execution risks
Strong customer-facing and technical communication skills
Demonstrated ability to coach, mentor, and develop engineering professionals
Strong organizational, communication, leadership, and project-management skills
Ability to balance technical quality, cost, schedule, manufacturability, and business objectives

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

The following qualifications are preferred and align with the previously discussed requirements:
Significant experience in industrial automation and custom equipment design

Strong background in mechanical design and engineering

Experience with robotics and hard automation

Experience with hydraulic and pneumatic systems and related controls

Familiarity with controls automation components and systems

Experience establishing engineering design standards and reusable engineering practices
Experience with engineering documentation, BOMs, revision control, and design-release processes
Experience working closely with machining, fabrication, assembly, electrical, commissioning, purchasing, and service teams

Experience participating in customer design reviews, technical discussions, FAT preparation, and installation or commissioning activities
Experience driving engineering process improvements and standardization
Ability to identify emerging technologies and determine their practical application within an automation environment

EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS:

There is flexibility around the exact number of years of experience. The priority is finding someone with the right combination of technical design expertise and engineering leadership experience

The ideal candidate will have:

Significant hands-on engineering design experience

Proven engineering management or leadership experience

Experience leading engineers while maintaining a strong understanding of the technical work being performed
A background that demonstrates progression from technical engineering/design responsibilities into leadership and management

Candidates who have only managed engineering teams without meaningful hands-on design experience may not be as well suited for the role. Likewise, highly experienced designers without demonstrated leadership and people-management experience may not fully meet the needs of the position.

The strongest candidates will be able to understand the technical details, lead the engineering team, manage project execution, and make sound engineering and business decisions.

KEY LEADERSHIP AREAS:

Engineering Leadership:
Lead and develop a multidisciplinary engineering organization while establishing clear priorities, accountability, technical standards, and performance expectations
Project Execution:
Ensure engineering resources, milestones, budgets, technical requirements, and deliverables remain aligned throughout the project lifecycle
Technical Excellence:
Maintain high standards for engineering quality, safety, manufacturability, documentation, and technical integrity
People & Organizational Development:
Develop engineering talent, strengthen technical capabilities, establish succession depth, and create a culture of ownership and continuous improvement
Business & Commercial Accountability:
Ensure engineering decisions support project profitability while balancing technical requirements, customer expectations, schedule, quality, and cost

COMPENSATION & WORK ENVIRONMENT

Salary
: $115,000–$125,000 per year

This is an onsite Engineering Director position in Schertz, Texas
, with responsibility for leading an engineering team of approximately 8 direct reports
.

7:30 AM–4:00 PM

based on customer availability and project requirements.

If you're an experienced engineering leader who combines hands-on design expertise with proven management experience
, this is an opportunity to make a significant impact
Bring your engineering design background, automation expertise, leadership experience, and project execution skills
to an organization delivering customized industrial solutions from concept through manufacturing, assembly, commissioning, and customer delivery
If you're ready to lead a multidisciplinary engineering team while driving technical excellence, accountability, and continuous improvement, we'd love to hear from you

jobs.title: Technical Director, PLM Platform Engineering
jobs.description:
The Estée Lauder Companies Inc.
is one of the world’s leading manufacturers, marketers, and sellers of quality skin care, makeup, fragrance, and hair care products, and is a steward of luxury and prestige brands globally. The company’s products are sold in approximately 150 countries and territories under brand names including: Estée Lauder, Aramis, Clinique, Lab Series, Origins, M·A·C, La Mer, Bobbi Brown Cosmetics, Aveda, Jo Malone London, Bumble and bumble, Darphin Paris, TOM FORD, Smashbox, AERIN Beauty, Le Labo, Editions de Parfums Frédéric Malle, GLAMGLOW, KILIAN PARIS, Too Faced, Dr.Jart+, the DECIEM family of brands, including The Ordinary and NIOD, and BALMAIN Beauty.

Description

The Director, Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) Platform Engineering is responsible for defining and executing the engineering strategy, platform governance, modernization, and long-term evolution of the enterprise Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) platform supporting global Research & Development, Product Development, Quality, Manufacturing, and Regulatory business capabilities.

Reporting to the Executive Director, ERP & Value Chain Platform Engineering, this role provides strategic leadership for the engineering realization, lifecycle management, and continuous improvement of the enterprise PLM platform while ensuring alignment with business priorities, enterprise architecture standards, and enterprise technology strategy. The Director partners closely with Product and Technology leaders, Enterprise Architecture, Enterprise Business Services (EBS), Operations & Infrastructure, Cyber Security, and strategic technology partners to deliver secure, scalable, and reliable PLM capabilities that enable product innovation and lifecycle management across the enterprise.

This leader will play a key role in the organization's PLM modernization strategy by providing technical leadership during enterprise platform evaluations, solution assessments, vendor demonstrations, technical proof-of-concept activities, and implementation planning supporting the selection and adoption of future-state Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) PLM solutions. The role requires practical experience with enterprise PLM implementations, modernization initiatives, and migration strategies from legacy or custom PLM environments to enterprise-grade platforms.

The Director is responsible for ensuring the PLM platform effectively supports the broader enterprise application landscape by enabling efficient collaboration across upstream product development processes and downstream enterprise capabilities, including ERP, Manufacturing, Quality, and Regulatory systems. Success in this role requires balancing strategic platform modernization with engineering excellence, operational stability, platform scalability, and long-term business value.

The ideal candidate combines deep expertise with enterprise Product Lifecycle Management platforms such as Dassault ENOVIA, Siemens Teamcenter, SAP PLM, or similar enterprise-grade solutions, along with demonstrated success leading complex PLM transformations, platform engineering organizations, and large-scale enterprise technology initiatives.

Key Roles & Responsibilities

Platform Strategy, Ownership & Lifecycle (35%)

Own the platform roadmap, lifecycle strategy, modernization initiatives, and long-term evolution of the enterprise Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) platform supporting global Research & Development, Product Development, Quality, Manufacturing, and Regulatory business capabilities.
Develop and execute platform strategies that improve scalability, engineering efficiency, business value, and long-term technology sustainability while aligning with enterprise architecture standards and organizational priorities.
Provide technical leadership for the evaluation, selection, and adoption of enterprise Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) platforms, including solution assessments, technical proof-of-concept activities, implementation planning, and migration strategy.
Develop enterprise migration strategies that enable the successful transition from legacy or custom Product Lifecycle Management solutions to modern Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) PLM platforms while minimizing business disruption and preserving critical product lifecycle information.
Lead the Enterprise Platform Engineering organization's engagement with the selected System Integrator (SI) throughout the implementation of the enterprise PLM platform, providing technical direction, engineering governance, design oversight, implementation guidance, and quality assurance while ensuring successful knowledge transfer, operational readiness, and long-term platform sustainability.
Establish enterprise engineering standards, platform roadmaps, lifecycle plans, modernization strategies, and technical governance that enable the organization to maximize the long-term value of the PLM platform.
Partner with Enterprise Architecture to ensure PLM platform capabilities align with enterprise technology standards, engineering principles, security requirements, and long-term architectural direction.

Key Roles & Responsibilities (Continued)

Platform Ownership & Delivery Governance (30%)

Provide strategic oversight for engineering realization across Enterprise Business Services (EBS), strategic technology partners, and the Enterprise Platform Engineering organization, ensuring high-quality delivery, platform stability, and operational excellence.
Establish engineering governance, release management, platform lifecycle management, environment strategy, and delivery standards supporting enterprise PLM capabilities.
Establish and mature the long-term engineering operating model for the enterprise PLM platform following implementation, including engineering governance, release management, platform lifecycle management, technical standards, enhancement delivery, and effective partnership with Enterprise Business Services (EBS).
Ensure engineering solutions are scalable, maintainable, secure, and aligned with enterprise quality standards while supporting long-term platform sustainability.
Ensure GxP-relevant PLM capabilities, implementations, and lifecycle changes adhere to established Computer System Validation (CSV), quality management, data integrity, and regulatory requirements throughout the platform lifecycle.
Govern validation readiness and execution for GxP-relevant platform implementations and changes, ensuring appropriate risk-based validation, qualification, requirements traceability, testing, documentation, deviation management, and release approval processes are completed in partnership with Quality and Validation teams.
Ensure validated PLM capabilities remain in a controlled state throughout their lifecycle, including upgrades, patches, configuration changes, integrations, releases, and environment migrations.
Drive platform optimization through continuous improvement, technical debt reduction, engineering automation, platform modernization, and operational efficiency initiatives.
Manage platform risks, engineering dependencies, technology roadmaps, software lifecycle planning, and technical decision-making to ensure long-term platform success.

Key Roles & Responsibilities (Continued)

Product Partnership & Platform Realization (20%)

Partner with Product and Technology leaders to define platform priorities, engineering roadmaps, modernization strategies, and long-term investment plans supporting enterprise Product Lifecycle Management capabilities.
Collaborate with Enterprise Architecture, Operations & Infrastructure, Cyber Security, Enterprise Business Services (EBS), business stakeholders, strategic technology partners, and the selected System Integrator (SI) to successfully deliver enterprise PLM capabilities and modernization initiatives.
Partner with Quality, Validation, Regulatory, Cyber Security, and other appropriate stakeholders to ensure GxP-relevant platform capabilities meet applicable validation, compliance, security, and data integrity requirements.
Ensure the PLM platform effectively supports enterprise business processes while enabling seamless interoperability with upstream product development processes and downstream enterprise capabilities, including ERP, Manufacturing, Quality, and Regulatory systems.
Provide engineering leadership for major platform initiatives, ensuring technical quality, delivery excellence, operational readiness, and successful business adoption.
Balance business priorities, engineering capacity, platform sustainability, and modernization objectives while driving continuous improvement across the PLM platform.

Key Roles & Responsibilities (Continued)

Engineering Leadership, Platform Excellence & Organizational Capability (15%)

Build and develop a high-performing engineering organization by mentoring engineering leaders, strengthening technical capabilities, fostering innovation, and promoting engineering excellence across the PLM platform.
Lead Enterprise Business Services (EBS), strategic technology partners, and the Enterprise Platform Engineering organization through clear engineering governance, technical leadership, delivery accountability, and organizational alignment.
Champion modern engineering practices, AI-enabled engineering capabilities, automation, reusable engineering assets, and continuous improvement to enhance engineering productivity, platform quality, and organizational effectiveness.
Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, continuous learning, and engineering excellence while developing organizational capability to support the long-term success of the enterprise PLM platform.
Promote knowledge transfer, technical documentation, and engineering standards that ensure long-term platform sustainability and organizational readiness.

Qualifications

Enterprise Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) Leadership & Platform Expertise

Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Technology, Product Development, or a related technical discipline.
8+ years of progressive leadership experience governing enterprise Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) platforms, engineering applications, or enterprise technology organizations within complex global enterprises.
Demonstrated experience leading engineering organizations responsible for enterprise PLM platforms supporting Research & Development, Product Development, Manufacturing, Quality, and Regulatory business capabilities.
Deep understanding of enterprise Product Lifecycle Management processes, platform architecture, product structures, engineering change management, configuration management, and product development workflows.
Proven ability to develop long-term platform strategies that balance business priorities, technical sustainability, modernization objectives, engineering capacity, and operational excellence.
Experience supporting global Consumer Packaged Goods (CPG), Manufacturing, Life Sciences, or similarly complex multinational organizations is strongly preferred.

Qualifications (Continued)

Enterprise PLM Modernization, Implementation & Engineering Leadership

Demonstrated experience leading or providing technical leadership for an end-to-end enterprise Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) implementation, including platform evaluation, solution selection, engineering realization, legacy data migration, deployment, and post-implementation operational transition, is strongly preferred.
Proven experience evaluating and implementing enterprise Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) Product Lifecycle Management platforms such as Dassault ENOVIA, Siemens Teamcenter, SAP PLM, PTC Windchill, Oracle Agile PLM, or similar enterprise-grade solutions.
Experience providing technical leadership during enterprise platform evaluations, solution assessments, technical proof-of-concept activities, implementation planning, and vendor selection initiatives

Collette is looking for a Director, Digital Analytics Architecture and Engineering
to join our growing Engineering Team. This is a hybrid role based at our headquarters in Pawtucket, RI .

About Collette: Let Us Show You the World!

There has never been a better time to be in the travel industry. See the world, connect with others, and experience the immersive benefits of one of the trendiest industries when you join the Collette team! As the longest-running tour operator in North America, our family-owned business leads the industry in innovation and expertise. Collette’s passionate team works hard to fulfill travel dreams and is always looking for talent that will help to shape the company’s future. Being part of the Collette team means having a willingness to grow, a desire to learn and ask questions, and a zest for seeing the world. From giving back to local communities to creating incredible experiences for a world of travelers and being part of a value-oriented team that cares for one another – Collette is all about the people. So, what are you waiting for? Your journey starts here.

Job Summary:

The Director, Digital Analytics Architecture and Engineering owns the strategy, architecture, governance, delivery, support, and optimization of the data layer and tagging architecture across the company’s websites, applications, user portals, and downstream marketing systems. This leader defines the blueprint for how customer and behavioral data flows from digital experiences through standardized data layers into tag management systems (TMS) and other downstream platforms. They establish the long-term technical direction and operating model for the digital analytics ecosystem, ensuring that the architecture is scalable, compliant, and capable of producing reliable, actionable data for lead intake, sales generation, and customer experience decisions. This is a new role for Collette, and this person will be responsible for standing up a new architecture for our Digital Products Systems.

This leader aligns product engineering, marketing, analytics, and operations around a shared digital analytics strategy, portfolio priorities, delivery commitments, and measurable outcomes. They establish decision-making and escalation mechanisms, communicate progress and risk to senior stakeholders, and sequence complex initiatives across multiple phases when necessary.

The Director serves as the senior technical authority for the company’s digital analytics ecosystem, including its websites, applications and user portals, data layer architecture, user-driven events, tagging standards, tag management systems (TMS), consent controls, and downstream integrations. They define architectural principles, data contracts, naming conventions, and engineering standards; guide significant technical decisions; and ensure that data moves through the ecosystem securely, consistently, reliably, and sustainably.

Primary Functions:

Define and maintain the end-to-end digital analytics architecture, documenting how customer and behavioral data flows from websites, applications, and user portals through standardized data layers into tag management systems (TMS), analytics platforms, and downstream marketing integrations.

Document change-management decisions and proposed roadmap changes.
Translate business and compliance needs from marketing team into clear technical requirements.
Turn complex technical requirements into quarterly projects and sequence tasks realistically to meet deadlines.
Facilitate alignment among web engineers, marketing analysts, product management and digital analytics, ensuring stakeholders are informed throughout project planning and execution.
Create comprehensive testing plans which include stakeholders’ acceptance testing phases.
Own tracking, consent and data usage requirements; ensure these are included into each project across digital platforms.
As projects bring systems online, coordinate with operations and support teams to identify run-state requirements, support models, handoff needs. Identify production risks so projects are scoped with ongoing ownership in mind.
Lead and develop a management structure that may include managers responsible for distinct areas of digital analytics engineering. Set clear accountabilities, coach leaders, assess organizational capacity, support succession planning, and evolve team structure and skills as the digital analytics portfolio grows.

Knowledge & Skills:

Demonstrated expertise in modern digital-platform architecture across websites, applications, user portals, frontend and backend services, standardized data layers, tag management systems (TMS), and third-party marketing integrations, with the ability to document current-state data flows, define scalable target-state architecture, and set technical direction.
Experience partnering with product management and senior stakeholders to create product and technical roadmaps, govern change decisions, evaluate tradeoffs, and translate strategy into realistic quarterly delivery plans.
A track record of leading complex, cross-functional initiatives across engineering, marketing, product management, digital analytics, privacy, and operations, establishing clear requirements, decision rights, milestones, and accountability for outcomes.

About Us

Girl Scouts of the USA

Founded in 1912, Girl Scouts of the USA (GSUSA) is the preeminent leadership development organization for girls and the leading authority on their healthy development. Millions of Girl Scout alums across the country and the world have gone on to achieve incredible things and make a tremendous impact in fields ranging from public policy, medicine, journalism, and athletics to international relations, science, technology, art, and entertainment.

As a mission-driven organization, Girl Scouts of the USA champions girls as they explore their worlds, try new things, and develop the courage, confidence, and character to make the world a better place. From stargazing during a first overnight camping trip to building robots, navigating a rocky hiking trail, working together on a community project, and learning about the importance of environmental stewardship, Girl Scouts of all backgrounds and abilities can unapologetically be themselves as they rise to meet new challenges and discover the issues that matter most to them. Along the way they learn the power of friendship, connection, and teamwork.

Girl Scouts are doers, innovators, problem-solvers, creators, and dreamers, and the GSUSA team is here to center, support, and inspire them, working with 111 local councils across the country and USA Girl Scouts Overseas to deliver our life-changing Girl Scout Leadership Experience.

The Technology community sets technology vision, strategy, goals, and performance measures to fulfill and advance the Technology Council Offerings that support the Movement’s business objectives. Technology directs traditional information technology functions, as well as enhances business value with innovative, technology-based solutions.

The VP provides leadership and oversight to define technology architecture, guide platform engineering, and ensure operational excellence across systems, integrations, and vendor-delivered solutions. This includes responsibility for AI-enabled workflows, as well as coordination with external managed service providers (MSPs) to deliver consistent, high-quality solutions aligned with GSUSA standards. Technology Strategy & Leadership

Align technology investments with GSUSA mission, business priorities, and financial constraints

Enterprise AI Agent Builder Framework (v1)
Business Process Automation & AI Transformation Strategy
Process Engineering Roadmaps (domain-specific transformation plans)
Reference Architecture for Agentic Systems (AI, data, integration, and UI)
MSP Enablement Standards (AI Framework, UI/UX, and integration guidelines)
Platform reliability, performance, and operational excellence metrics

AI Platform & Agent Builder Framework

Design and define the enterprise Agent Builder Framework for creating, deploying, and managing AI agents
Establish standards for agent orchestration, tool integration, memory, and governance
Develop reusable components, templates, and reference architectures for scalable agent development
Serve as the central design authority for agentic AI and early-stage AI transformation initiatives

Business Process Automation & Engineering

Develop and lead the enterprise-wide business process automation and process engineering strategy for AI-enabled workflows
Identify and prioritize high-value automation opportunities across business domains
Define human-in-the-loop models and decisioning frameworks for agent-assisted workflows
Create structured process engineering roadmaps aligned to transformation priorities

Platform Engineering & Architecture

Establish foundational architecture for AI platform services, orchestration layers, and enterprise systems
Define integration patterns across CRM/ERP systems, cloud platforms, and AI services
Ensure alignment between front-end experience layers and backend AI and data platforms

External MSP & Vendor Management

Manage relationships with external technology vendors and managed service providers (MSPs)
Define standards for UI/UX, APIs, and integration for externally delivered solutions, including React-based applications
Ensure vendor-delivered products are on time, within budget, and aligned with specifications and architecture standards
Provide technical expertise to procurement efforts and vendor negotiations

Culture, Enablement & Change Leadership

Foster a high-performing engineering culture focused on innovation, collaboration, and continuous improvement
Promote knowledge sharing and technical learning across the organization
Lead organizational change initiatives supporting adoption of AI and automation-driven ways of working
Enable internal teams and partners to effectively adopt new frameworks and platforms
Support inclusive practices in technology design, development, and delivery
Ensure alignment with GSUSA’s affirmative action and nondiscrimination commitments

Partners with Product Managers, Operations, Index Delivery & Management, Architecture, UX and other stakeholders to translate business priorities into pragmatic technology solutions and delivery plans

jobs.title: Sr. Engineering Manager, Core Services - Slack
jobs.description:
To get the best candidate experience, please consider applying for a maximum of 3 roles within 12 months to ensure you are not duplicating efforts.

Job Category

Software Engineering

Job Details

About Salesforce

Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.

Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

Slack is looking for an Engineering Manager on the Core Services engineering team. The purpose of this role is to keep Slack working seamlessly at massive scale — it's the infrastructure that keeps Slack feeling lightning fast. This person will be a steward of some of the most critical, high-throughput systems at Slack — the kind of work where doing it well means millions of users, at the world’s most important and interesting companies, never experience a hiccup.

About The Opportunity

We operate at tremendous scale with systems that process millions of events per second. Our team maintains and builds performant services that include:

Edge Caches
Realtime Services
Enterprise Key Management (EKM)
International Data Residency (IDR)
Image Uploads, Downloads, and Proxying

We've done our job correctly when none of our users think about us, much like a vital utility. We don't typically ship new user-facing features, but rather ensure our systems are exceptionally performant, highly available, reliable, and scalable. In other words, we make Slack work seamlessly. Slack's backend services are written in Go and Java, and Slack's API is built on PHP/Hack.

The Core Services Team

We are a team building critical services that enable Slack to scale for our largest customers. Our edge caches power the most latency-critical queries for our largest entities today, serving approximately 35% of all Slack API traffic. Our Realtime Services (RTS) power Slack's core messaging stack — running 10 services, 4 of which are mission-critical Tier 0 services — ensuring that messages, presence, and real-time events are delivered reliably at scale. We also own services that power Slack's Enterprise Key Management and International Data Residency features, enabling Slack to win and retain enterprise and government customers with strict compliance requirements (FedRAMP/NIST).

We have a strong commitment to quality and understand that simplicity and reliability are the foundations of our work.

We are actively building the future of edge services at Slack, so we can support a growing number of globally distributed customers with their compliance requirements with minimal latency.

What You'll Be Doing:

Owning the technical direction and roadmap across the Core Services portfolio: Edge Caches, Realtime Services, Enterprise Key Management, International Data Residency, and Image Proxying and Uploads. You’ll have large footprint and the opportunity to drive major impact. And you'll decide what to invest in now, what to sequence later, and what to decline — balancing reliability, migration, and new capability work.
Leading a multi-system migration of Flannel to Loom, our next-generation edge cache, while keeping the current systems running at full reliability for millions of users. You'll drive the team to ship new capabilities without introducing risk to infrastructure that people depend on daily.
Driving delivery and execution while maintaining reliability as a top priority, including sprint planning, product launches, incident follow-ups, operational sustainability analyses, and building the technical case for investment with leadership. You'll ensure the team doesn't trade reliability for velocity, but is always high-performing.
Owning on-call operations and incident management for Tier 0 services. You'll manage on-call rotations across partnering teams, triage production issues, lead incident response for your services, and drive improvements to runbooks, alerting, and operational tooling.
Partnering cross-functionally with Product, Sales, Compliance, Security, AWS, and other infrastructure teams on dependencies, timelines, and risks. You'll be the shortest path to solutions — whether it's unblocking a compliance audit for South Korea, coordinating IDR region launches with Sales and AWS, or negotiating priorities with partner teams for shared work.
Representing your team's work in leadership reviews, quarterly and annual planning, and executive forums. You'll build compelling business-and-technical cases for your team's investments and tell your leadership what's really going on early enough that nothing becomes a fire drill.
Building and maintaining a high-trust team culture where engineers do impactful work and grow. You'll hire well, manage performance with fairness and transparency, mentor emerging technical leaders, and celebrate your team's wins.
Managing cost and capacity for services that run at massive scale, working with finance on AWS spend trends, exec-approved budget increases, and cost-saving initiatives like the Loom migration (projected $1-2M savings).
Driving the team to adopt AI development tooling for maximum impact, while maintaining engineering rigor and quality for critical infrastructure.

You're Our Person If:

You've led engineering teams for 5+ years building and operating high-scale, high-availability backend infrastructure or distributed systems.
You have strong software engineering fundamentals with previous experience as a Senior+ backend engineer, with enough depth to be credible in architecture discussions about caching, distributed systems, observability and reliability best practices, and system design — and to build SME knowledge in a new area fast.
You have a history of managing Tier 0 / Tier 1 services where uptime matters deeply, including owning on-call rotations, leading incident response, and driving operational improvements.
You have experience with realtime messaging systems or event-driven architectures at scale — presence, message delivery, pub/sub, or similar systems where latency and reliability directly impact user experience.
You have experience leading multi-quarter migration or platform evolution projects while simultaneously keeping existing systems reliable.
You've managed teams through prioritization trade-offs — weighing reliability vs. feature work vs. cost vs. compliance — and can articulate those decisions to both engineers and executives.
You have experience partnering with cross-functional stakeholders (Product, Sales, Compliance, Security, Infrastructure) to turn business requirements into engineering plans.
You understand how to build a high-performing team culture: hiring, performance management, retention of top performers, and growing new technical leaders.
You have experience managing engineers across multiple time zones, with an async rhythm that doesn't depend on overlap hours.
An understanding of how and where AI software development tooling can be deployed for maximum team impact.

Even Better If:

You have experience with the Go and/or Java programming language at scale.
Experience with AWS infrastructure, including multi-region architectures.
Experience with Kubernetes and container-based deployments.
Experience working within highly regulated environments where an understanding of FedRAMP/NIST frameworks was essential.
Experience with Enterprise Key Management, data residency, or compliance-driven infrastructure.
You've managed teams responsible for Edge Caching, CDN, or API gateway systems.
You've led teams through system deprecation and migration while maintaining service reliability.

Unleash Your Potential

When you join Salesforce, you’ll be limitless in all areas of your life. Our benefits and resources support you to find balance and be your best , and our AI agents accelerate your impact so you can do your best . Together, we’ll bring the power of Agentforce to organizations of all sizes and deliver amazing experiences that customers love. Apply today to not only shape the future — but to redefine what’s possible — for yourself, for AI, and the world.

Accommodations

If you need a reasonable accommodation during the application or the recruiting process, please submit a request via this Accommodations Request Form .

Please note that Salesforce uses artificial intelligence (AI) tools to help our recruiters assess and evaluate candidates’ resumes and qualifications throughout the recruiting process. Humans will always make any candidate selection and hiring decisions. Please see our Candidate Privacy Statement for more information about how we use your personal data and your rights, including with regard to use of AI tools and opt out options.
